author: joshavant
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex users creating scheduled automations could successfully use connected apps in the creator turn, but the new job omitted that app authority and later scheduled runs could not call those apps. Senderless authenticated local operator turns could also lose the Automations tool before the exact creator-authority capability reached the cron mutation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex-native apps are not part of the generic dynamic-tool allowlist, so a tool-name-only cron cap cannot represent their authority. This change captures a private, versioned `codex.apps` authority envelope from the exact active creator thread, binds it to the prepared Codex profile and account, persists it with the job, and intersects it with current Codex app policy and inventory on every scheduled run. The stored envelope is always a ceiling: current policy, app availability, destructive-action policy, and approval policy may narrow it but never expand it.

Fresh creator authority is transported as an exact-run, one-use in-process capability. It exposes only Automations for an admitted senderless local operator turn, is consumed at the cron commit boundary, and is revoked on settlement or abort; it does not restore other owner-only tools or promote the caller to general sender ownership. Restart restoration, account mismatch, revoked/narrowed app policy, approval/elicitation refusal, and reauthorization diagnostics are covered explicitly.

There is no new user-facing configuration, Gateway protocol change, or SQLite schema-version bump. Runtime-private authority now lives in a same-version, first-use SQLite companion row rather than `job_json`, so older writers can rewrite recognized job fields without erasing it. The row is bound to a versioned fingerprint of the authority-relevant tool-runtime inputs; downgraded cap changes, malformed authority, and explicit cap replacement fail closed to visible reauthorization instead of reviving stale authority. Existing jobs created without a captured app envelope continue ordinary non-app behavior; a job that needs Codex app access must be explicitly recreated or reauthorized from a fresh authenticated owner turn.

## User Impact

New Codex-created automations retain the connected apps and permission ceiling available when they were created, survive Gateway restart, and can use those apps during unattended scheduled execution without gaining later-added apps or broader permissions. Failures caused by account changes, revoked apps, narrower policy, or unavailable approval/elicitation paths now stop visibly with recovery guidance.

Documentation now describes scheduled Codex app authority, current-policy intersection, restart behavior, and the explicit reauthorization path for existing affected jobs.

## Evidence

- Exact-head persistence-hardening autoreview at `fe13cb276f4a`: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — TruffleHog clean; no accepted/actionable findings; patch judged correct (`0.97`).
- Source-equivalent changed-surface Testbox: [Actions run 31460600898](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31460600898) — all generated-contract, core/core-test/extension/extension-test typechecks, lint, schema, database-first, dead-code, boundary, and import-cycle guards passed.
- Downgrade/storage Testbox: [Actions run 31464854470](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31464854470) — 267/267 focused cron and state-schema tests passed, including upgrade → old-writer rewrite → re-upgrade preservation, cap-drift retirement, no-resurrection, malformed-row recovery, atomic rollback, read-only loading, fresh recapture, and cascade deletion.
- Final direct guard Testbox: [Actions run 31465054094](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31465054094) — 150/150 focused tests, core/core-test typechecks, full core lint, and generated Kysely verification passed. Its sole final nonzero was the Kysely guard requiring the raw-DDL rationale immediately above the feature-local `CREATE TABLE` call; that comment-only placement was corrected, then Kysely guardrails, generated type verification, and the native v6 schema guard passed locally.
- Focused regressions: core agent-tool authority tests, Gateway admission/lifecycle matrix, and Codex configured-MCP/app authority suites passed. The final post-rebase Gateway pair passed `385/385`; removing the selective exact-run Automations retention reproduced the pre-fix failure before the final repair was restored.
- Build: `pnpm build` passed on the exact dirty-tree implementation before commit.
- Live authenticated E2E with a fresh isolated ChatGPT OAuth profile and real Codex app:
  - Gateway hello confirmed `operator.admin` for the direct local creator turn.
  - Codex `thread/start.dynamicTools` contained `automations`, and the model invoked it rather than shell/CLI fallback.
  - The stored job had versioned `codex.apps` authority, exact profile/account identity, 5 captured apps, and 41 captured app tools.
  - Authoritative Codex `item/completed` MCP evidence showed the exact proof-app call count advance `1 → 2 → 3` across creator preflight, first forced run, and post-restart forced run, with zero failed or sibling app calls.
  - Both scheduled runs completed `ok` with the expected marker; authority restored after a same-state/config/port Gateway process restart; the proof job was removed.
  - The live implementation tree was pinned to base `75a454469de9` with dirty diff hash `09037fca30b08da013a81677fdc9141598fcc5a34a5cd5af13b2020f7f6ace29`; the subsequent rebase integration is covered by the final-head focused and Testbox gates above.
  - Sanitized local verdict: `/private/tmp/openclaw-cron-app-e2e-v4-proof-20260810/verdict.json`. Credential-bearing state and raw model logs were deleted, and the isolated OAuth profile was logged out and removed.
- Direct sibling Codex runtime-contract inspection confirmed `item/completed` is the authoritative MCP-call lifecycle event and carries the `mcpToolCall` server/tool/status fields used by the live proof (`codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:308`, `codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1510`). The exact pinned Codex 0.147 runtime also enforces app/MCP approval before invocation and routes it through MCP elicitation or the legacy user-input path, never generic command-execution approval (`codex-rs/core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:1278`, `codex-rs/core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:1398`, `codex-rs/core/src/mcp_tool_call.rs:1432`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:681`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:720`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:767`).

## Change Size

- Production: `+1813/-216` (net `+1597`)
- Tests: `+1707/-39` (net `+1668`)
- Documentation: `+37/-0`
- Generated SDK baseline: `+110/-110` (net zero)

The production growth implements the missing private authority contract and its lifecycle owner boundaries: versioned capture/validation, one-use exact-run admission, downgrade-stable cron persistence, authority-input binding, current-policy intersection, Codex thread restoration, fail-closed diagnostics, and cleanup/revocation. The additive companion table is necessary because the previous `job_json` envelope is rewritten by older full-row writers; keeping the authority there cannot satisfy downgrade safety. It does not add a public config or protocol surface.

author: julienlegoux
body:
Closes #32

Issue bundle: [`docs/epics/epic-0-skeleton-hardening/issues/10-stdout-write-failures.md`](https://github.com/julienlegoux/external-reviewer/blob/issue-32-stdout-write-failures/docs/epics/epic-0-skeleton-hardening/issues/10-stdout-write-failures.md)

## What changed and why

Two ways `io.WriteString(stdout, report)` escaped the done-line seam, and one
sentence in the documents that a partial write made false.

**SIGPIPE no longer kills the process.** `Run` now registers for
`syscall.SIGPIPE` (`handleSIGPIPE` in `internal/cli/run.go`). `os/signal`'s
documented rule is that with no registration, a write to a broken pipe on
fd 1 or 2 raises SIGPIPE and the process dies by signal, while the same write
on any other descriptor merely returns `EPIPE`; registering flattens that
special case so every such write comes back as an ordinary Go error. A signal
death runs no deferred function, which is exactly why `review … | head -20`
exited `141` with the transcript cut off before `done`.

`syscall.SIGPIPE` is defined on Windows too and `signal.Notify` accepts it
there (where it is simply never delivered), so **this needs no `//go:build`
divergence at all** — one code path, compiled and executed on both matrix OSes.

**A failed write is now classified rather than treated as all-or-nothing.**
`writeReport` in `internal/cli/review.go` splits the two facts a failed write
can carry:

- nothing written — stdout is still empty and the caller has no report;
- N bytes written — the caller holds a fragment that looks exactly like a
  report. Those bytes cannot be unwritten and an output file is forbidden
  (SPECS § Interfaces), so the error names the report incomplete with the
  bytes written and the report's full length.

A short write reported with a `nil` error (an `io.Writer` breaking its own
contract; `os.File` cannot produce one) folds into the same class, because
returning `nil` for a report that was never fully delivered is the one outcome
the calling skill cannot recover from.

Both go out through `diag.WriteError` via `runReview`'s existing default
branch — one `error:` line, `stop=failed`, exit `2`. Nothing routes around the
seam issue #29 built.

## Which documents changed and why

Both places the invariant was written down said *"stdout is empty on any
failure"*, which a partial write makes false:

- **`docs/planning/SPECS.md` § Interfaces** — restated as the three-part
  guarantee the shipped code actually holds (nothing reaches stdout until the
  final message is complete; the process never dies by signal; a failed write
  is announced on stderr naming the report incomplete). Also names the
  `head -20` case explicitly, and adds "a report that could not be written to
  stdout" to `failed`'s enumeration in the `stop=` closed set.
- **`docs/planning/CONVENTIONS.md` § Error handling** — the same correction,
  since it restates SPECS 12.

**No new stop-reason word was invented.** `failed` already covers "reached and
then unusable for any other reason"; the amendment only makes its enumeration
list this case.

The same statement is restated in `resolveAndReview`'s doc comment, and
`TestRun_StdoutFailsMidReport_NamesTheReportIncomplete` /
`TestRun_ClosedStdoutPipe_NeverDiesBySignal` assert what it claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Written test-first, black-box through `Run`, with the failing stdout
      supplied as an `io.Writer` the test controls (`failingStdout`).
- [x] A stdout writer returning `syscall.EPIPE` produces exit `2`, a `done`
      line and exactly one `error:` line —
      `TestRun_StdoutRefusesEveryByte_ExitsTwo`. *(Honest note: this one passed
      against the pre-change code, since an in-process writer cannot raise a
      signal; it is a regression pin. The signal half is the pipe test below,
      which was genuinely red.)*
- [x] `external-reviewer review <repo> --prompt "…" | head -20` exits `0`, `1`
      or `2` with a `done` line on stderr and never `141` — verified by hand on
      a real Unix shell (see below) **and** as an automated two-OS test.
- [x] A stdout writer that accepts N bytes and then errors leaves the run at
      exit `2` with a `done` line and one `error:` line naming the report
      incomplete —
      `TestRun_StdoutFailsMidReport_NamesTheReportIncomplete` (plus
      `TestRun_StdoutShortWriteWithoutError_IsStillIncomplete` for the
      nil-error short write).
- [x] The invariant is stated in the code and in SPECS § Interfaces in a form
      true of the shipped behaviour, and tests assert what it claims.
- [x] The success path is untouched —
      `TestRun_SuccessfulReport_ReachesAPlainWriterIntact` asserts the report
      arrives byte for byte through a bare `io.Writer` in exactly one `Write`
      call at exit `0`; the pre-existing
      `TestRun_SuccessfulTurn_WritesFinalTextVerbatim` still passes unchanged.
- [x] No `//go:build`-divergent behaviour ships — there is none; the one path
      is exercised on both matrix OSes by
      `TestRun_ClosedStdoutPipe_NeverDiesBySignal`, which selects its
      expectation at runtime (`ProcessState.ExitCode() < 0` means killed by a
      signal on Unix; Windows has no SIGPIPE and simply fails the write).
- [x] `golangci-lint run` passes; CI is the authority for
      `go test ./... -race` (see "Testing").

## Testing

`golangci-lint run ./...` and `gofmt -l .` were run inside a fresh
`core.autocrlf=false` clone of the branch — **0 issues, no unformatted files**.

**Windows** (`go test ./...`): 3 packages ok, **80 tests passing, 2 skipped**
(the live-model round trip and the closed-pipe child half, both skipped by
design when their env vars are unset).

**Linux** (`GOOS=linux` cross-build of all three test binaries, run under a
real Linux kernel): `internal/cli`, `internal/diag`, `internal/reviewer` all
**PASS**.

`go test ./... -race` could not be run locally (no cgo toolchain on the dev
machine) — CI is the authority for it.

### The `| head -20` criterion, by hand on a Unix shell

Run against a `linux/amd64` build, with a real `head -20` closing the read end.

**Before this change** — the bug, reproduced:

```
EXIT=141
model   openai-codex/gpt-5.5  auth=OAuth
turn 1  tools=0  in=4 out=43000  $8.6004  0.3s
```

No `error:` line, no `done` line: the process was killed by SIGPIPE mid-write.

**After this change**:

```
exit code = 2
model   openai-codex/gpt-5.5  auth=OAuth
turn 1  tools=0  in=4 out=43000  $8.6004  0.3s
error:  writing the report to stdout: the report on stdout is incomplete, 65536 of 172000 bytes were written: write /dev/stdout: broken pipe
done    turns=1  in=4 out=43000  $8.6004  0.3s  stop=failed
```

`65536` is the Linux pipe buffer — a genuine partial write, not a synthetic
one, and exactly the case the incomplete-report diagnostic exists for.

`TestRun_ClosedStdoutPipe_NeverDiesBySignal` is that same scenario as an
automated test (child process, real pipe on a real fd 1), and it was observed
**failing on Linux before the fix** with `signal: broken pipe`.

## Size

408 insertions / 16 deletions — ~424 changed lines against the issue's ~250 M
estimate, and well under the ~1000 split threshold. The overrun is the
two-OS subprocess harness (`TestBrokenStdoutPipeChild` plus its parent,
~110 lines with comments), which the issue costed as part of "the signal
handling and its two-OS test"; the production change itself is ~40 lines.

## Bookkeeping

Also reconciles issue 07 (PR #39, merged) to `done` and moves issue 10 to
`in-progress`/`pr-open` in the bundle, per the issue-implementation flow.

author: evanharmon1
body:
## What

Vendors an executable readiness gate and a scoped read-only `gh api` wrapper into the shepherd skill, and rewires SKILL.md §6 to invoke the gate instead of hand-assembling the evidence.

- **`ai/skills/universal/shepherd/assets/readiness-gate.sh`** (new): `check --repo owner/repo --pr N --head <40-hex adjudicated SHA> (--codex-state FILE [--codex-actor-id N] | --codex-disabled) [--allow-edited-root ID]...` evaluates every §6 readiness condition fail-closed against fresh, guarded, page-safe fetches (`--paginate --slurp` into a standalone `jq`, every capture exit-checked): PR `OPEN` and still draft; live head equal to `--head`; every check GitHub reports for the commit concluded non-failing — evaluated **twice** (entry + immediately before the verdict), page-safe from the commit's own check runs and deduped legacy statuses, an **empty** list indeterminate, `skipping`/`neutral` neutral; `reviewDecision` not `CHANGES_REQUESTED`; `mergeStateStatus` none of `DIRTY`/`BEHIND`/`UNKNOWN` — **`BLOCKED` (and `DRAFT`) are promotable; the gate never requires `CLEAN`**; every `## Deferred findings` entry ticked **and** carrying a real outcome (`fixed in <sha>` / `declined: <rationale>` / `filed as …#n`; bare `declined:` settles nothing; all sections aggregated; child headings stay inside; continuations must be indented); §2's reply-linkage predicate ported verbatim (`unanswered`/`new-follow-up` hard-fail; `edited-since-reply` reported distinctly, clearable only via explicit repeatable `--allow-edited-root` — the named-exception rule); where Codex cloud review is enabled, the sibling `check-codex-cloud-review.sh check` must exit clean (invoked, never reimplemented), against an attempt state first **proven to name this exact repo, PR, and head**. The promotion fingerprint is **double-read**: computed over the exact content the conditions judged, then every surface re-fetched fresh and required identical (`content-moved` otherwise, naming the changed surfaces) — so a mid-gate edit fails before `gh pr ready` notifies anyone. Read order is terminal: evaluated fingerprint → fresh content compare → second checks evaluation → scalar re-read (state/draft/head/reviewDecision/mergeStateStatus) as the last network read → local emit. Exit 1 = first failed condition (stable machine token + sentence, e.g. `checks-pending`); exit 2 = indeterminate (failed fetch, malformed payload, empty check list, `UNKNOWN` mergeability) — unknown never passes, and the codes are documented in the header.
- **`audit` mode** (same script): the identical evaluation with the draft requirement inverted (target must be non-draft) — §2's unexplained-promotion reconcile branch and §6's already-non-draft paragraph need "does this head independently pass the full gate" answered without hand-rolling, and `check` rightly refuses non-drafts. An `audit` pass never authorizes `gh pr ready`. The `fingerprint` subcommand recomputes the five-surface hash with no gate attached — the post-promotion compare read.
- **`ai/skills/universal/shepherd/assets/gh-ro.sh`** (new): a structurally GET-only front door for `gh api`. Allowlist vetting — one **relative** REST endpoint (absolute `://` URLs refused: `gh api` honors them verbatim, which would reach internal/metadata services), `--paginate`, `--slurp`, `--jq/-q` (detached or `--jq=`), explicit `GET` only — and refusal of everything else by name: `-f/--field/-F/--raw-field/--input` (fields also flip gh's default method to POST), any non-GET method, attached short forms (`-XGET`, `-q.login`), unknown flags, and the `graphql` endpoint (GraphQL rides POST and can carry mutations; the skill's GraphQL read lives inside readiness-gate.sh — the choice is documented in the wrapper's usage text). Execs `gh api --method GET` with vetted args; propagates gh's exit code.
- **SKILL.md**: frontmatter `allowed-tools` grants exactly the **two write-incapable** asset scripts — `Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/assets/gh-ro.sh:*)` and `Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/assets/readiness-gate.sh:*)` — via the documented skill-directory substitution; `check-codex-cloud-review.sh` is deliberately **not** granted (its `reserve`/`attach`/`reap` write and delete local state at caller-chosen paths), so §2's cycle invocations keep prompting. §6's hand-assembled snapshot recipe and inline `promo_fp` are replaced by the gate invocation plus post-promotion `fingerprint` re-compare (with an explicit far-side head re-read, and a promote-immediately rule: a prompt-held promotion requires a fresh `check`); the non-mechanical reasoning stays (why BLOCKED is promotable, the ready_for_review-automation blocker, the human-configured Codex knobs, undo once-then-stop). §6 net line count went down, 246 → 245: the removed recipe and its four load-bearing bullets bought back almost exactly what seven adversarial/verification rounds added in invocation and contract prose — measured, not estimated. §2's raw read calls (timeline guard, comment fetches, the predicate snippet) route through the wrapper; the intro caveat states the grant, the `CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR` convention for harnesses without the substitution, and the residual prompts.
- **Tests**: `scripts/test-shepherd-readiness.sh` (53 cases), wired as `task test:shepherd-readiness` inside `verify` like the existing suite: a fixture per failing condition asserting nonzero + the condition token; indeterminate fixtures (fetch failures, empty check list, `UNKNOWN` merge state, missing/mismatched Codex state, helper exit 2) asserting exit 2, never pass; BLOCKED+REVIEW_REQUIRED passes; full-pass fingerprint printed, stable across two runs, and reproduced by `fingerprint`; mid-gate races (head moved, promoted, CHANGES_REQUESTED, DIRTY, late-red checks, body edit, late top-level comment) each caught at the right stage; deferred-parser hardening; audit-mode contract; no-GNU-timeout fallback under a restricted PATH; gh-ro refusal matrix (methods, fields, unknown/attached flags, graphql, absolute URLs, multi/no endpoint) plus GET pass-through with exact forwarded args and exit-code propagation. `gh` is stubbed on PATH; the gate runs as a byte-identical copy beside a stubbed Codex helper to pin the helper-exit mapping.

## Why

**#384**: while shepherding PR #380, a session-authored gate printed the failing `lint`/`verify` checks in its snapshot output and then ran `gh pr ready` anyway — nothing wired the displayed states to an exit, and a hand-assembled gate enforces exactly the conditions its author remembered that day. The readiness gate is the one-way door of the lifecycle, so every condition must be enforced by something runnable and tested. The third acceptance criterion — a failing or pending required check can no longer be printed-and-promoted past — is now `checks-failing`/`checks-pending` exiting 1 before any fingerprint exists to print, evaluated a second time immediately before the verdict.

**#385** (maintainer decision 2026-08-10, scoped wrapper): `Bash(gh api:*)` would remove every prompt but pre-approves a prefix whose POST forms mutate — an allowlist entry cannot constrain arguments. gh-ro.sh is the prefix that structurally cannot write, so it can be granted narrowly; raw `gh api` (writes and GraphQL) keeps prompting — friction, never silent.

## Allowed-tools decision and residual prompts

The grant uses `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` — substituted in both the frontmatter rules and the skill body, so prescribed invocations resolve to the literal vendored path at whichever root the skill lives (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `ai/skills/universal/`). Deliberately **not** used: a `Bash(gh api:*)` grant (mutation-capable prefix), leading-wildcard path patterns (`Bash(*/assets/gh-ro.sh:*)` would match any planted path), and any grant on the Codex classifier (local-write-capable subcommands). body:
## Summary

`boto3` and `urllib3` are pinned in **both** `pyproject.toml` and `requirements.txt`. Renovate manages the two files as separate managers, so PR #271 raised boto3 to `1.43.68` in `pyproject.toml` and left `requirements.txt` on `1.43.67`.

**Nothing failed.** CI and the Makefile install from `requirements.txt`, so the tests ran against `1.43.67` while the package metadata claimed `1.43.68`. Neither file is wrong on its own terms, which is why no gate objected.

`pyproject.toml` already carried a comment asking for `jsonschema` to be kept equal across the two files. That is the shape of the problem: a convention written in a comment is not a convention anything enforces, and the first automated change broke it.

## Changes

- `requirements.txt`: boto3 → `1.43.68`, matching `pyproject.toml`
- `scripts/check_runtime_pins_agree.py`: compares the shared names, wired into `validators.yml` (PR gate) and `make drift`
- Merged the two open Renovate PRs (#271 boto3 1.43.68, #272 hypothesis 6.165.3)

### What the check deliberately does not flag

Only **shared** names are compared. `aws-xray-sdk` is optional and lives in `requirements.txt` alone; treating a one-sided declaration as drift would make the check fail on the repository as it is meant to be.

Two other ways it could produce a false answer are covered by tests:

- `requirements.txt` carries long comment blocks, including a version that was deliberately rejected. Reading `# jsonschema==4.17.3` as a pin would invent a disagreement.
- A range is not a pin, so there is no version to compare. The pinning policy is enforced elsewhere; this check is only about the two files agreeing.

## Testing

- [x] Confirmed the gate **fails on the tree as it was before the fix** (exit 1, naming both versions and both files) and passes after. A new gate that has not been seen refusing anything is not yet evidence of anything.
- [x] `make lint` clean, `make drift` no failures, `make test-quick` 43 passed
- [x] `scripts/tests` — 402 passed, 9 of them new
- [x] `zizmor .` no findings; `check_actions_pinning.py` PASS
- [x] PII grep over the diff — only the documented placeholders

## Blocked Features

None.

author: ecuthiell
body:
## What

Make the `bd worktree` command family establish the current directory as its Git repository boundary before command discovery can consume inherited routing state.

A shared `internal/gitenv` helper classifies repository, index, object-store, namespace, executable, template, and `GIT_CONFIG*` routing variables with POSIX/Windows key semantics. The startup config probe runs with those variables scrubbed, and the first root pre-run operation clears them in-process for worktree descendants. Worktree-owned Git subprocesses retain the same scrub as defense in depth.

## Why

Setting `cmd.Dir` on the eventual Git subprocess is too late. Startup config initialization runs before Cobra dispatch and invokes `git -C`; inherited `GIT_DIR` and related variables can override that explicit directory and select a decoy shared-worktree config. Root pre-run discovery can then populate process-wide Git and `RepoContext` state before a worktree command's `RunE` begins.

The startup probe is the only pre-hook Git discovery path, so it uses the shared scrubber while preserving its explicit repository argument as authority. The first root pre-run operation then removes the same routing variables from the CLI process for worktree descendants. Clearing in-process preserves the original PID, OS signal semantics, cancellation context, exit status, arguments, current directory, and standard streams; a supervised child re-exec would weaken those process guarantees.

Environment-key matching is case-sensitive on POSIX and case-insensitive on Windows. Non-routing controls such as `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` and `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS` are preserved for create, list, info, and status. Worktree removal keeps its deliberate stricter policy and pins `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` only inside its removal runner.

## Validation

- Real `bd` binary dispatch with a valid decoy `.beads/.env` and poisoned repository, worktree, index, object, namespace, executable, and config routing
- Create/list/info/remove stay in the target repository, and list asserts the target `BeadsState`
- Create from a target with no `.beads` refuses without changing its path, worktree registry, or `.gitignore`
- A malformed config reachable only through linked-worktree routing produces no startup warning and cannot influence target `worktree list`
- Mutation check: removing the startup-probe scrub makes that malformed-decoy regression fail on the leaked config warning
- In-process boundary test proves routing keys are removed while non-routing variables are preserved and inherited test state is restored
- POSIX/Windows key semantics, hook/template suppression, and stricter removal controls

Fixes #5531

body:
홈 화면 바로가기(iOS)와 Android 아이콘을 `AI/AX NEWS FEED` 로고로 교체합니다.

## 변경 사항

### 아이콘 5종 생성
`assets/icon-source.png`(1254×1254)를 원본으로 생성했습니다.

| 파일 | 크기 | 용도 |
|---|---|---|
| `public/apple-touch-icon.png` | 180×180 | iOS 홈 화면 |
| `public/icon-192.png` | 192×192 | manifest |
| `public/icon-512.png` | 512×512 | manifest |
| `public/favicon-32.png` | 32×32 | 브라우저 탭 |
| `public/favicon-16.png` | 16×16 | 브라우저 탭 |

모든 아이콘은 **알파 채널 없이** 생성했습니다. 알파가 있으면 iOS 홈 화면에서 배경이 검게 렌더링됩니다.

### `public/manifest.json` 신규
이름·설명은 기존 `metadata.json`과 동일하게 맞추고, `theme_color`는 브랜드 컬러 `#ff2e98`을 사용했습니다.

아이콘은 `purpose: "any"`로만 선언했습니다. `maskable`로 선언하면 Android가 가장자리 약 10%를 잘라내는데, 여백을 줄인 현재 크롭에서는 `NEWS FEED` 글자가 잘립니다.

### `index.html` 링크 태그 추가
`icon` 32/16, `apple-touch-icon` 180, `manifest`, `apple-mobile-web-app-title`, `theme-color` 추가.

### `icon-source.png`를 `public/` 밖으로 이동
`public/` 하위는 전부 빌드 산출물로 복사되는데, 원본(810KB)은 어디서도 참조되지 않으면서 그대로 배포되고 있었습니다. `assets/`로 옮겨 빌드에서 제외했습니다.

- `dist` 총 크기: **1.6MB → 808KB**

### 파비콘은 슬래시 심볼로 별도 크롭
`AI/AX NEWS FEED` 전체 워드마크는 3.45:1 비율이라 16px로 줄이면 글자당 3px가 되어 판독이 불가능합니다. 그래서 32/16만 브랜드 심볼(`/`)로 따로 크롭했습니다.

슬래시는 위쪽이 오른쪽으로 기울어(y=395에서 x=681, y=693에서 x=580) `AX`의 `A` 발과 x축 범위가 겹치기 때문에 사각 크롭으로는 분리되지 않습니다. 슬래시 bbox를 잘라낸 뒤 픽셀 단위로 남은 네이비 조각을 배경색으로 치환해 분리했습니다.

`apple-touch-icon`과 `icon-192/512`는 워드마크 크롭을 그대로 유지합니다.

## 크롭 방식
로고가 가로로 긴 워드마크(1036×469, 약 2.2:1)라 정사각형을 왜곡 없이 채울 수 없어, 로고 중심 기준으로 크롭해 가로폭의 88%를 차지하도록 맞추고 원본의 좌우 여백 비대칭(125px/93px)을 보정했습니다.

## 범위 밖

author: allyblockcast[bot]
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip coordinates queued agent runs against mutable issue state.
> - A queued run is intentionally cancelled with `issue_terminal_status` when its issue reaches `done` or `cancelled` before dispatch.
> - Recovery used to read that cancellation as a lost execution path, blocking and reassigning an intentionally-closed issue.
> - This branch originally fixed that by exempting the marker at the common stranded-escalation boundary.
> - Review correctly blocked that approach: the marker is evidence about the *run*, and `getLatestIssueRun()` keeps returning it after a legitimate reopen, so an unconditional exemption suppressed recovery for that issue forever.
> - While this branch sat, `d7c28c3a0` landed the correct fix on master from the other direction — it clears the stale marker inside `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues` and restores the issue's normal liveness path.
> - The source change here is therefore superseded and has been dropped. What remains is the one acceptance criterion master still does not assert.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

- Refs Paperclip issue [BLO-25411](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-25411).
- Superseded by `d7c28c3a0` ("fix(recovery): resume reopened terminal dispatches"), which is already on master.
- Related precedent: #1035 handles benign routine duplicate-suppression cancellations; #824 handles checkout-adoption handover cancellations.

## What Changed

Reduced to a single regression assertion; **no production code changes remain**.

- Extend the queued-run terminalization regression through the recovery sweep: queue a dispatch, terminalize the issue before the run starts, observe `issue_terminal_status`, then assert the issue is not escalated, reopened, reassigned, or commented on.
- Dropped from the earlier revision of this branch:
  - the `escalateStrandedAssignedIssue` early return (superseded by `d7c28c3a0`, and the subject of the blocking review finding);
  - the direct escalate-level test — master's sweep-level `re-dispatches an issue reopened after terminal dispatch cancellation` covers the reopen half more faithfully, asserting `continuationRequeued: 1`.

Why this assertion is still worth keeping: master's convergence suite contains no reference to `reconcileStrandedAssignedIssues`, `recoveryService`, or `issueRecoveryActions`, so the *terminal* half of the contract is currently unpinned. Master's own test covers only the reopened half.

## Verification

Run on this branch (rebased onto `98bb6bacc`):

- `vitest run server/src/__tests__/heartbeat-queued-backlog-convergence.test.ts -t "terminal"` → 1 passed.
- `vitest run server/src/__tests__/issue-recovery-actions.test.ts` → **80 passed**, including master's `re-dispatches an issue reopened after terminal dispatch cancellation`.
- `tsc --noEmit -p server/tsconfig.json` → clean.

On the previous head `e6f2a5789`, `General tests (server 3/4)` failed two `heartbeat-retry-scheduling.test.ts:2639` cases (`executionRunId` was `null` where the test expected it retained). Those were **not** caused by this branch and are **fixed by the rebase**:

- reverting `recovery/service.ts` to the pre-PR base `1eab22741` and re-running still reproduced both failures (2 failed / 63 passed), so the branch's own change was not implicated;
- the same file on current master runs **74 passed / 0 failed**.

## Risks

- Test-only change; no production code, schema, migration, UI, telemetry, or public API changes.
- The assertion pins existing master behaviour that is already verified green, so it cannot change runtime behaviour — it can only fail if that behaviour regresses.

## Model Used

- Anthropic `claude-opus-5[1m]`; tool use and code execution enabled. (The earlier revision of this branch was authored with `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`.)

author: martyinspace
body:
## What

The `seed = A ⊕ B` construction from `docs/recovery-model.md`.

- **A** = 32 random bytes (hub share). Not a Shamir share, never counted in any threshold.
- **B** = `seed ⊕ A`, then Shamir-split across `friendCount` shares at threshold 2.
- Both halves mandatory: node alone can never recover, all friends together can never recover.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `recovery-split.ts` | Added `splitBytes`/`combineBytes` — raw bytes-level Shamir API beside the existing phrase-level one. Same Shamir core, no fork. Phrase-level signatures unchanged. |
| `two-layer-split.ts` | **NEW.** `splitTwoLayer(seed, friendCount)` → `{ hubShare, friendShares, seedChecksum }`. `combineTwoLayer(hubShare, friendShares, checksum)` → seed. |
| `index.ts` | Added `two-layer-split.js` export |
| `two-layer-split.test.ts` | **NEW.** 28 tests asserting the handover invariants |
| `recovery-split.test.ts` | Extended with `splitBytes`/`combineBytes` tests |

## Integrity check

`combineTwoLayer` with wrong/corrupt shares would produce a different valid Ed25519 seed — the worst failure mode. A 4-byte SHA-256 checksum over the seed catches this and throws `TwoLayerCombineError` instead.

## Key test: collusion resistance

The test that proves the XOR layer is load-bearing (not decorative):

```
ALL friends, NO hub → Shamir-combine yields B, not the seed
```

A flat Shamir split would pass every round-trip test but fail this one.

## Constants

`TWO_LAYER_THRESHOLD = 2` is a new constant. `RECOVERY_THRESHOLD = 3` is untouched — the sovereign/phrase path still uses it.

## Does NOT touch

Enrolment, keeper panel, server, UI — that's Step 4b.

## 背景
阶段三（WS-25）限流加固的非阻断跟进项（WS-31）：多副本/真实网关部署前收敛 XFF 信任，并为已鉴权的昂贵接口叠加用户维度限流。

## 改动
1. **XFF 信任收敛**：新增 `TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED`（默认 `false`）。关闭时一律用直连地址（`get_remote_address`），忽略客户端传入的 `X-Forwarded-For`，防止伪造/轮换 XFF 绕过注册、登录的暴力破解限流；开启时才采信 XFF 首个 IP。
2. **已鉴权接口按用户维度限流**：`/api/fitness/assess`、`/api/fitness/plans/generate`、`/api/payment/orders` 改用 `user_or_ip_key`——能解析出登录用户时按 `user:{id}` 计数，凭据缺失/无效回退 IP。NAT 后不同用户不再共用同一 IP 配额互相误伤，单用户也无法靠换 IP 绕过。阈值仍走 `RATE_LIMIT_*`。
   - 技术取舍：未采用 slowapi 堆叠 IP+user 两个 limit 的写法——堆叠为 AND 语义，外层全局 IP limit 仍会在 NAT 下误伤，与目标相悖；单一智能 key 才同时满足「NAT 不误伤」与「单用户滥用命中 429」。
3. **小清理**：移除 `app/utils/images.py` 中未使用的 `guess_extension()`（及 `Path` 导入）；为注册/登录 429 用例补上真实的 `Retry-After` 头部断言（原断言为空操作）。

## 测试
新增 7 项，全量 `pytest -q` **53 passed**：
- `trusted_proxy` 开/关下 `client_ip` 取值与注册接口行为（伪造 XFF 关闭时不绕过、开启时按 XFF 独立计数）
- `user_or_ip_key` 对有效/缺失/无效凭据的 key 选择
- 已登录下单接口：同 IP 不同用户不误伤、单用户（含轮换 XFF）用尽配额命中 429

## 配置/依赖
- 新增环境变量 `TRUSTED_PROXY_ENABLED`（默认 false，已在 `.env.example` 说明开启条件）。
- 无新增依赖，无数据库迁移。

## 不做
- 未引入 Redis（`MemoryStorage` 单实例兜底不变；多副本另开任务切 `storage_uri`）。

author: dcbaugher
body:
Fixes the `docs` workflow, which has been **failing on `main`** since #58 merged. RTD itself is fine — it built `0dacf99` successfully and <https://docs.engin.bio> now renders example outputs correctly. This is CI only.

## What broke

Two changes in #58 collided with each other. The cache-refresh step committed the cache and then could not push it:

```
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
remote: - 8 of 8 required status checks are expected.
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch hook declined)
```

The same PR made those eight checks required. A bot push satisfies none of them, so the step could never have worked on a protected branch.

## Why not just let the bot bypass

That fixes the symptom by weakening the protection that just started doing its job. Better to invert the design: **CI verifies the cache rather than maintaining it.** No write permission, nothing to bypass, and the invariant is enforced by a failing check — which is the project's own stated preference over a habit that has to be remembered.

## How the check works

The RTD-parity build moves **first**, so it runs against the cache exactly as committed, before the executing build refreshes it. myst-nb's own logging distinguishes the two cases:

| situation | log line |
|---|---|
| cache hit | `Using cached notebook: ID=1` |
| stale or missing | `Executing notebook using local CWD` |

The step greps for the second and fails with instructions to rebuild and commit. **Tested both directions** rather than assumed: clean against the current cache, and tripped by editing an executed page without refreshing it.

This also removes a churn problem the pushing version would have had — the cache's SQLite index changes on every build even when no output does, so the bot would have produced a no-op commit on every push to `main`. That is visible in the failed run: `1 file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

## Contributor-facing

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now says to commit the refreshed `docs/.jupyter_cache` alongside any change to an executed page, explains why it is committed at all, and warns that the index shows as modified regardless. The CI failure message says the same thing, so forgetting is a clear error rather than a puzzle.

Also tightened the lint line to say `ruff check .` on the whole tree — checking a narrower scope than CI is what let the ruff failure in #58 through in the first place.

author: timberking1190
body:
Closes the launch-blocking item G3 in `LAUNCH-ACCEPTANCE.md`.

## The problem

The sign-up gate was hardcoded:

```ts
limit: 5,   windowMs: ONE_HOUR   // per IP
limit: 50,  windowMs: ONE_HOUR   // global
```

Both **fail closed**, and that is the part that matters. A family that trips one does not see a rate limit. They see an error, and they conclude CMBA's registration is broken.

**The global cap of 50/hour was the dangerous one.** CMBA runs 589 teams, implying thousands of registrations. At 50 per hour it takes *days* of perfect utilisation to register the association once. On Sept 1 it would have throttled the real launch inside the first hour while every dashboard still read healthy, because from the server's point of view refusing traffic is not an error. That is the worst shape a bug can have on a launch day: invisible to you, and visible to every family.

**The per-IP cap of 5 was quietly wrong too.** One household registering three children plus two parent accounts is five. A normal family hit it exactly. A shared connection carrying a few families (community centre, school, an ISP using CGNAT) blew through it immediately.

## The change

New defaults **20 per IP per hour** and **2000 globally per hour**, both env-overridable via `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT_IP` and `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL`, so they can be widened on the day without a code change.

A malformed, zero or negative override **falls back to the default rather than being obeyed** — a typo setting the limit to `0` would otherwise refuse every registration in the association. That case is unit-tested.

## How to read these numbers

This is **not** the primary bot defence and should not be treated as one. Turnstile is enforced on sign-up whenever `TURNSTILE_SECRET` is set (verified live in production — an unchallenged POST returns `Bot challenge failed`). A challenge every caller must pass beats a global counter that cannot tell a family from a bot.

So: the **per-IP** limit is the real control against a single source. The **global** limit is a backstop against a catastrophic distributed event, and should be generous enough that only such an event reaches it.

**The specific numbers are a judgment call and worth your sanity check** against what you actually expect on Sept 1. They are now a dial rather than a cliff, which was the real defect.

## Safe to land now

Public registration is currently closed, so these limits are inert until the Sept 1 flip reopens it. Landing it now means it soaks with everything else rather than being a launch-week change.

## Verification

70 test files, 650 tests (up from 69/643), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean, `gitleaks protect --staged` no leaks.

## Minors'-data safety

No migration, no schema change. No access-control change: the gate's authorisation logic is untouched, only the numeric thresholds move. No new public path to personal data. No logging change.

author: jacobpoteet
body:
Closes #101.

Inside the Activity, a player's Discord profile now shows what they're playing and how they're doing:

```
Playing Lunch Special
Today's Special · No. 26      ← the game mode (Leftovers / Chef's Choice)
Guess 3 of 6                  ← progress
02:14 elapsed
```

A finished round reads `Solved it in 4 guesses` or `Out of guesses`, and the timer drops off — a counter still climbing beside a solve is measuring how long the tab stayed open.

### It never names the dish

A profile is read by people who haven't played today, so the answer, the guessed dishes and the clues are all barred from those two lines — the same rule as never leaking the target except via `/reveal`. Progress is safe; a guess count says nothing about what the dish is. A test sweeps the fold's entire output space against a character class no dish name survives.

### One OAuth scope, and it isn't an identifying one

`setActivity` is gated behind `rpc.activities.write`, so presence is the first thing in the app that genuinely needs OAuth. It asks for that one scope and **not** `identify` or `guilds`, so the anonymous model survives whole — nothing here learns who the player is, and localStorage remains the only state.

The code-for-token exchange needs the app's client secret, which must never reach the browser, so it hops through the Worker at `POST /api/discord/token`. An unconfigured deployment answers 503 and loses nothing but the presence line — presence is a flourish on someone else's profile and the game never waits on it.

### Shape

| Piece | What it owns |
|---|---|
| `shared/presence.ts` | PURE fold: round → the two lines. Unit-tested (8 tests). |
| `src/discord/presence.ts` | Authorization + throttled `setActivity`. No-op off Discord. |
| `worker/routes/discord.ts` | The code→token hop. |
| `GamePage` | One effect keyed on round status + guess count, gated on `tracked`. |

Authorization runs once per page load (`prompt: "none"`, silent for repeat players) and a refusal is sticky — re-asking on the next guess is harassment. Updates are deduped by serialized payload and throttled to one per 4s, because Discord's RPC limit is 5 SET_ACTIVITY per 20s and a burst would drop the *interesting* update (the win) rather than the noise.

`attachPresence(sdk)` is registered inside the handshake's own `.then()`, **not** on the branch that wins the 5s mount race. That cap decides when React mounts and nothing else; gating a feature on it is what silently killed the share button on every slow Activity start.

### Verified

- `npm test` — 270 passing, 8 of them new
- `npx tsc -b --force` — clean
- `POST /api/discord/token` against the dev server: 503 unconfigured, 400 on a missing or oversized code, 502 when Discord rejects the code. The failure log carries the status only — the response body echoes the submitted code back.
- **Not verified:** the presence card itself, which needs the game running inside real Discord (`npm run tunnel` + the portal URL mapping).

### Before this ships

Presence stays off until the Worker has the credentials from the Discord portal's OAuth2 page:

```bash
npx wrangler secret put DISCORD_CLIENT_ID
npx wrangler secret put DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Both keys are in `deploy.yml`'s placeholder `.dev.vars` line for the typecheck, and documented in CLAUDE.md and `wrangler.jsonc`. No portal toggle is needed — the scope is requested at runtime, and the card uses the app's own icon, so no Rich Presence art assets have to be uploaded.

author: dchaudhari7177
body:
Refs #126

## The bug

The issue names a gap that's reachable today, and it is real:

```java
if (storm.action() == StormLimiter.Action.STORM_LINE) {
    writer.append(renderer.stormLine(...));   // throws
    stormLimiter.confirmStormLine(...);       // skipped
    deduper.rollback(fingerprint);            // skipped
    return;
}
```

With the rollback sitting *after* the append, a failing storm-line write skips it and leaves `reportPending = true` for that fingerprint. `Deduper.decide` then answers `SILENT` for it (`Deduper.java:66-68`) until the dedup window rolls over — **the error stops being reported for ~5 minutes on the default window, and nothing goes red.**

## The fix

Move the rollback into a `finally`:

```java
try {
    writer.append(renderer.stormLine(...));
    stormLimiter.confirmStormLine(storm.suppressed()); // #57: clear only once written
} finally {
    deduper.rollback(fingerprint);
}
```

That is the invariant #51 actually wanted. The rollback is about *this error's own* report, which was never written on this path whether or not the storm line itself made it — so it should be unconditional. `confirmStormLine` stays inside the `try`, so #57's "clear only once written" still holds. The throw still reaches the outer handler, so the never-throw guarantee and the consecutive-failure parking are unchanged.

## The tests

New `ReportPipelineTest` in `stacktale-core`, asserting on **what reached the file** — the only thing a user of stacktale can observe:

- a written report is confirmed, and the repeat becomes a summary
- a storm-suppressed report is rolled back and still reports after the window
- **a failed storm-line write still lets the next occurrence report** ← the gap
- a failed storm line keeps its suppressed count for the next line (#57)
- `close()` drains the pending summary counts
- `process()` never throws, and parks after repeated write failures

**Red-before-green, per the TDD rule in CONTRIBUTING:** with the rollback moved back after the append, `aFailedStormLineWriteStillLetsTheNextOccurrenceReport` fails (1 report on file, not 2) and the other five still pass.

One detail worth flagging for future test authors: assertions are anchored to line starts, because the file header *documents its own delimiters* — a plain `contains("━━━ ERROR #")` matches the header comment as well as a real report. I got that wrong first.

## Two seams, both package-private

- **`forTesting(...)`** — `create()` cannot build a pipeline that is both active and unable to write: `ReportWriter`'s constructor probes the destination, and a failed probe becomes `isActive() == false`. Injecting the collaborators is the only way to reach the failure branches.
- **an injectable clock**, threaded through to `Deduper` and `StormLimiter`. Their windows are minutes long. `DeduperTest` and `StormLimiterTest` already inject a clock, so this follows the existing convention rather than inventing one.

The failure is injected through a `Renderer` that throws on `stormLine`, not a subclassed `ReportWriter` — `ReportWriter` is `final`, and the pipeline can't tell the two apart: both leave `STORM_LINE` decided with nothing on disk. Say the word if you'd rather `ReportWriter` grew a seam instead.

## Verification — please read

**Maven is not installed in this environment.** I compiled and ran the suite against the JDK directly (JUnit 6.1.1 + AssertJ 3.27.7 from the local repository, against the pinned 6.1.3).

- **117 of the 122 runnable core tests pass.**
- 5 fail: `EnvCollectorTest` ×1, `ReportRendererTest` ×4. **These fail identically on an unmodified `main` in the same setup** — I built pristine `main` from `git archive` to confirm it. They need Maven's resource filtering and the pinned 6.1.3.
- `JsonReportRendererTest` couldn't be compiled at all without Jackson.

So: the new tests and every test that could run are green, and the 5 failures are artifacts of my environment, not of this change. **CI is the real check.** I also could not run PIT for the before/after mutation score the issue asks for.

## Scope

Deliberately limited to `stacktale-core`. The issue's second half — the six knobs `LogbackXmlConfigTest` omits (`echoSuppressionMillis`, `containerLogger`, `emitReportsToLogger`, `maxReportsPerMinute`, `format`, `redactionCorrelation`) — lives in the `stacktale` module and is a separate logical change per the one-change-per-PR rule. Logback isn't available here to run it against either. Marked `Refs` rather than `Closes` for that reason; happy to follow up.

## Note on process

`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks contributors to claim an issue and wait for a reply first, and I did not — apologies. Happy to close this if you'd rather it went to someone who claimed it.

author: snake14
body:
### Description

Stacked on #44 — review that one first; this PR targets its branch, so the diff here is only the addition.

#44 analyses a plugin against `maximum_supported_matomo`. That never sees a plugin calling a core API which does not exist yet in the oldest Matomo its `plugin.json` claims to support: the call analyses cleanly against current core, and then fatals for everyone on an older install. This adds the leg that catches it.

- `matomo-targets` input, a JSON array of `{target, php}` objects defaulting to `[{"target": "minimum_required_matomo"}, {"target": "maximum_supported_matomo"}]`. The job becomes a matrix over it, so a caller can drop back to one target by passing a single-element array. `php` is optional and falls back to the `php-version` input; set it per target once a plugin's targets span Matomo majors, because `bootstrap-phpstan.php` executes core rather than only parsing it and a Matomo 6 checkout cannot be bootstrapped by the PHP 7.2 Matomo 5 still allows. The workflow compares the resolved PHP against the checked-out `piwik_minimumPHPVersion` and fails with that instruction rather than dying on 8.1 syntax partway through analysis.
- `artifacts/bootstrap-phpstan.php`, copied into the Matomo root when the checkout has none.
- The result cache key now includes the target, since the legs analyse different Matomo trees and both save within one run.

**Why the bootstrap copy is needed.** Matomo only ships `bootstrap-phpstan.php` from **5.4.0** (added 2025-03-01, first released in that tag), and plugin `phpstan.neon` files reference it as `bootstrapFiles: ../../bootstrap-phpstan.php`. Against an older target PHPStan exits before analysing anything, so without this the minimum leg would fail to start for every plugin whose declared floor predates 5.4.0 — which is most of them; CustomReports declares `>=5.0.0-rc5`. The file has to be copied into the Matomo root rather than referenced from the action checkout, because it derives `PIWIK_DOCUMENT_ROOT` from its own location. Its three dependencies (`core/bootstrap.php`, `core/Application/Environment.php`, `core/Exception/NotYetInstalledException.php`) are all present in the 5.0.0-rc5 tag, so the copy works against the oldest target in use.

**Expect this to surface real findings.** The point is to fail where a plugin has been relying on newer core, so some plugins will go red on the minimum leg when they adopt this. The two valid resolutions are the same as everywhere else: stop using the newer API, or raise `require.matomo` in `plugin.json` and note it in the changelog. `matomo-targets: '[{"target": "maximum_supported_matomo"}]'` unblocks a plugin while that is sorted out.

This is the PHP half of the same problem as #48, which catches the Less and Twig half at test time. Neither covers the other: a PHP call fails only when the code path is reached, so tests can miss it, while plugin `.less` and `.twig` compile at runtime and take down every page.

Related: PG-5221, PG-4897.

author: stranske
body:
## Why

The archive kept every work's sidecar in **two** trees — `staging_sidecars/` and `Art/works/<wid>/` — with the second *declared* canonical and the first the one this store actually read. Nothing held them together, so they drifted: by 2026-08-09 they disagreed about work identity on 142 works, and `Q547923` sat on 1 staging sidecar against 50 archive ones.

The damage was not the drift. It was that **every audit check read staging too, so all of them reported clean while the canonical tree held the defects** — including five artist misattributions, one of which put Rembrandt van Rijn on a Rembrandt *Peale* portrait.

The workspace has now collapsed the two trees onto `Art/works` and quarantined the other (its `DECISIONS.md` → **D020**, 2026-08-10), merging per field rather than copying — `subject` led in staging on 2,221 works, while `category`, 20 `filter:*` exclusion tags across 16 works, and a history event were correct only in the archive. So this store's default now names a directory that no longer exists.

## What changed

- `store.STAGING` → `store.WORKS`, resolved by a new `_works_dir()`.
- New **`FAA_WORKS_DIR`**. `FAA_STAGING_DIR` is still honoured as a fallback so a deployment that sets it keeps starting — but it now points at nothing, so anything still setting it should move to the new name. (Nothing currently sets it: no launchd plist, shell profile, or environment on the operating host.)
- Default is `DEFAULT_ART_WORKS_ROOT`, which `config.py` already defined — so the app now finds the real archive by default instead of a repo-relative path that never existed.
- Docstrings corrected: the module opened with *"Store backed by staging_sidecars/"*, which is what made the two-tree split easy to miss.

## Test gate

`TestOneSidecarTree` in `tests/test_companion_app_config.py` pins the **default** tree.

Nothing pinned it before. Every other test in that file sets `FAA_STAGING_DIR` explicitly, so none of them ever exercised the default — and the default is exactly what broke.

**Verified by deliberate break:** restoring the old `REPO_ROOT / "staging_sidecars"` default left the rest of the file green and failed *only* the two new tests; reverting returns the suite to green. Full suite **995 passed, 11 skipped**, coverage 80.5%.

author: heysanil
body:
Follow-up to #33. Answers "is there any reason we can't uncap `MAX_FILES_PER_ARCHIVE`?" — the honest answer is that the file count was a proxy for a resource nobody bounded, so raising it means bounding the real one.

## Why the file limit wasn't protecting anything

- **It was never a measured constraint.** 64 arrived with the Turborepo conversion (`07fbbb1e`) as an advertised-but-unenforced number; `dfe389bb` only made the existing value binding. Nobody derived it from a limit.
- **It isn't a security control, by its own admission.** The gate's comment states a client can evade it by claiming `encrypted` or sending unparseable metadata, and encrypted shares are unenforceable *by design* — the count only exists inside E2E ciphertext. It restrained honest clients only.
- **The zip format isn't the limit either.** client-zip 2.5.0 emits Zip64 overflow markers, so the classic 65,535-entry ceiling doesn't apply.

## What actually needed bounding

The metadata blob. It is stored in Redis, re-served by `/metadata/:id` on **every** download-page load, declared as an unbounded `t.String()` on `/upload/complete`, and Bun caps request bodies at **128 MB** by default. A single POST could park megabytes behind one file id no matter what the file count said.

| New limit | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_METADATA_BYTES` | 512 KiB | Rejects an oversized blob at `/upload/complete`, **before** the file-count gate and before any S3 completion. Unlike the file count, it also covers encrypted shares |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` | 4 MiB | `serve.maxRequestBodySize`. File bytes go straight to S3, so this API only ever receives JSON; the largest legitimate body is an `/upload/complete` carrying `MAX_PARTS` ETags (~600 KB) plus metadata |

`MAX_FILES_PER_ARCHIVE` goes 64 → 1000. A config test pins the invariant that a full 1,000-file archive (~420 bytes/entry with 255-char names) still fits under the byte cap, so the two knobs can't drift into a state where the client gate accepts a selection that then fails at completion.

Because the client gate added in #33 reads the server-advertised value, **the limit can be tuned further via env var with no frontend release**.

## Browser E2E in CI

The Playwright suite has never run in CI — `.github/workflows/test.yml` had no Playwright job. So the `webkit` project added in #33 only guarded regressions for whoever remembered to run it locally, which is exactly how a total Safari upload outage shipped green. Adds a `Browser E2E (chromium + webkit)` job with `--with-deps` browser installs and a report artifact on failure.

## Verification

- New route tests fail against the pre-fix code (2 MiB metadata returns 200 and is stored) and pass after, including the encrypted case the file-count gate is blind to, and asserting the rejection happens before `completeMultipartUpload`.
- 550 backend + 38 shared + 702 frontend unit tests, 8/8 e2e across chromium + webkit locally, typecheck and biome clean.

- enforce that exact version in both the local static-server smoke and the post-deploy GitHub Pages smoke

## Why
The live smoke currently only checks that `home.json.dataVersion` is non-empty. A stale CDN response or older deployed artifact could therefore pass even when the repository is publishing a newer data snapshot. Exact version matching turns stale/mixed deployments into an explicit CI failure.

## Validation
The expected-version path is exercised by PR CI through the existing local HTTP smoke after a full static export. The deployed workflow uses the same helper after merge.

## Scope
Deployment/data-contract verification only. No Pokémon retention decisions, UI, CSS, routing, or browser interaction behavior changes. No real-device validation is required if CI passes.

author: tomohisa-masaki
body:
## 背景

`claude-guard.sh` (PreToolUse hook) が **URL を文字列として含むだけの無害コマンドまで deny** していた。原因は「http クライアント語 + 対象ドメインがコマンド文字列に含まれる」という緩い判定。実際にこのセッションでは検証コマンドや `echo`/`git commit` で URL に触れる操作を誤ブロックし、**この改修 PR の作成コマンド自体も (PR 本文に例文リテラルを含むため) 旧 guard にブロックされた** — バグの実例そのもの。

## 修正

コマンドを**セグメント** (`|| && ; & | $( ` `` () <> {}`) に分割し、各セグメントの**「実際に実行される先頭コマンド語」**(env 代入・`sudo`/`command`/`env`/`nohup` 等のラッパーを剥がした後の語) がネットワーク取得コマンド (`curl`/`wget`/`xh`/`http`/`httpie`) のときだけ Figma/New Relic ドメインを判定する。`ln` 分岐も先頭語が `ln` のときのみ ask。

| 入力 | 旧 | 新 |
|---|---|---|
| 実際の取得コマンドで Figma/New Relic を叩く | deny | **deny** (維持) |
| env prefix / `sudo` / コマンド置換 / パイプ経由 | deny/一部漏れ | **deny** (すべて検出) |
| `echo` で URL を文字列として言及 | 🔴 deny | **allow** (修正) |
| commit メッセージに URL | 🔴 deny | **allow** (修正) |
| `grep <domain> file` | allow | **allow** |
| `echo` で `ln ~/.claude` を文字列として言及 | 🔴 ask | **allow** (修正) |
| 実際の `ln -sf … ~/.claude/…` | ask | **ask** (維持) |

fail-safe (jq 無し/parse 失敗/空 command は allow) は不変。

## 検証

- `bash -n` OK
- **単体テスト 13 ケース全合格**: deny 6 (env/sudo/コマンド置換/パイプ含む) / allow 5 (誤検知解消 3 含む) / ask 1 / fail-safe (壊れ JSON→allow)
- ⚠️ vLLM タイムアウトのため `/local-review` は未実施。狙い撃ちの単体テストで代替 (本改修は誤検知/検出漏れが論点なので単体テストが直接的な証拠)

反映は各マシンで `git pull` (hook が呼ぶ `scripts/claude-guard.sh` が更新される)。

body:
## Description
Resolves #9796

This PR introduces the frontend UI and mock pneumatic services for the Automated Overweight Axle Redistribution AI. One of the most archaic and physically dangerous tasks in trucking is manually sliding trailer tandems on the side of a highway to correct an overweight axle. This feature eliminates manual axle sliding by integrating directly with the truck's digital air suspension system. By reading the precise load on the Steer, Drive, and Tandem axles, the app dynamically adjusts the pneumatic airbag PSI to shift the freight's center of gravity, legally balancing the truck on the fly.

### Changes Made:
- **`axle_redistribution_model.dart`**: Established the `RedistributionSession` and `AxleWeights` schemas, mapping the strict DOT weight limits (12k/34k/34k) into a boolean `isLegal` getter that triggers the `targetPsiAdjustment`.
- **`axle_redistribution_service.dart`**: Implemented a mock `Stream` simulating a common scale-house failure scenario. The service detects an illegal 35,200 lb load on the drive axles, triggers a +14.5 PSI adjustment to the rear trailer airbags, and successfully shifts the weight to achieve a perfectly balanced, DOT-legal configuration.
- **`axle_redistribution_screen.dart`**: Built a mechanical engineering dashboard. The UI translates complex pneumatic telemetry into an easily digestible visual format. It utilizes dynamic progress bars that clearly highlight when an axle group is "OVER" capacity in red, and visually demonstrates the weight shifting in real-time until all bars return to a safe green state.

author: chodeus
body:
## Summary

Security + correctness hardening for the develop-only CL2K poster maker, from a structural review. Closes a Plex admin-token leak and an SSRF-to-Plex-admin path, fixes a 422 that broke the Poster tab for TVDB/IMDB-only titles, stops a title-less save from writing a `.jpg` dotfile, ends negative-caching of transient TMDB/ONNX failures, refuses to save un-erased art when AI removal is unavailable, and bounds season batches. Also restores the develop Dockerfile node base-image digest to match main.

## Related issue

N/A — hardening from a review sweep.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking)
- [ ] Breaking change (config migration, schema, endpoint, or UI behavior)
- [ ] Docs only
- [ ] Refactor / internal cleanup

## Details

**Security**
- `image_fetch.download`: raise hostname-only on HTTP failure — `requests`' `HTTPError` text embedded the full URL, leaking the minted `X-Plex-Token` into API error bodies. Also: scheme-aware token minting (never onto cleartext `http://` for an `https://` instance), cache key snapshotted before the mint, and raise on redirect-budget exhaustion (never cache a 3xx body as the image).
- `image_fetch`: reject non-artwork paths on a configured Plex host before the token is minted (initial URL + every redirect hop), mirroring the `/plex-art` proxy guard. Stops a request `backdrop_path`/`logo_path` from reaching `/:/scrobble`, `/library/.../refresh`, etc. with the admin token attached.

**Correctness**
- `GenerateRequest`/`SeasonsRequest`: `tmdb_id` is now optional but a validator requires it *unless* a backdrop is supplied — fixes the 422 on TVDB/IMDB-only titles without breaking TMDB art auto-source. `_require_any_id` now guards every save endpoint, and `_persist_poster` fails closed on an empty filename stem (no more `.jpg` dotfiles overwriting each other).
- `tmdb_art` and `text_detect._session`: stop memoizing transient failures (one blip no longer strips a title's art or disables the text detector for the whole process).
- `generate_for_item`: refuse when AI text-removal is requested but the provider is unusable, instead of silently saving un-erased art as "generated".
- Season batches: bound (max 60, rejected visibly not truncated) + dedupe requested seasons, and fail closed if the worker thread can't start.

## Testing

`MAGICK_HOME=… python -m pytest -k "cl2k or tmdb or text_detect or season or api_smoke"` — all green. New/updated regression tests cover each fix: token-not-in-error / redirect-exhaustion / scheme-mismatch (`test_cl2k_image_fetch`), Plex artwork-path allowlist (`test_cl2k_plex_art`), the tmdb-or-backdrop validator plus tvdb-only-with-backdrop happy path (`test_cl2k_assets_without_tmdb`), empty-stem guard (`test_cl2k_destinations`), AI-unavailable refusal (`test_cl2k_maker`), and season bound/dedupe/job-start (`test_cl2k_season_jobs`).

## Checklist

- [x] Config schema unchanged (`backend/util/config.py` untouched)
- [x] Frontend unchanged (backend + tests only)
- [x] No new `DAPS` references introduced
- [ ] Docs / wiki — behavior of the CL2K extension endpoints tightened; no shape change
- [ ] CHANGELOG — develop-only extension; release-please runs on main

## 문제

가운데로만 쌓아도 점수가 무한정 잘 오르는 문제. 스테이크 배당 `p/(1−p) × 0.9`이 위험 5%짜리 중앙 배치에도 매 턴 스테이크의 ~5%를 얹어줘서, 저위험 장기 생존 = 지수 복리가 됐고 체크포인트가 그걸 금고에 확정해줬음 — "안전한 복리 머신".

## 해법

배당률을 `max(0, p − stakeRiskFloor)/(1−p)`로 변경 (`stakeRiskFloor = 0.1`):

- **위험 10% 이하의 안전 배치는 스테이크 배당 0** — 블록 점수만 획득. 운명은 안전한 자에게 배당을 주지 않는다
- 걸린 점수가 커지면 중앙 반복 쌓기는 명백히 기댓값 마이너스 (HUD 기댓값 표시가 실시간으로 경고)
- 점수를 불리려면 문턱 위의 진짜 베팅(표식·오버행·무거운 블록)이 필요하고, 베팅의 하우스 엣지 때문에 탈출 타이밍 문제는 그대로 유지

author: juntaki
body:
## Summary

Wires `NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension`'s `createItem`/`modifyItem`/`deleteItem` (macOS On-Demand write path) through to the daemon's **existing** filesystem-watcher local-change/DAG admission path -- no File-Provider-specific sync engine.

Design: the extension writes bytes to disk with ordinary `FileManager` operations (exactly like any app would), then sends a new `LocalWriteRequest` shell-IPC message carrying only `local_path`/`relative_path`/kind -- no content, no metadata. The daemon resolves the link, looks up its running `LinkRuntime`, and calls `LinkFlushHandle::capture_local_write`, which constructs an `FsChangeEvent` and calls `LocalChangeProcessor::process_event` -- the exact same call a live filesystem watcher's own event triggers. The daemon never trusts the OS-supplied `contents`/metadata; it re-observes the live file itself.

`FileProviderItem.capabilities` now advertises `.allowsWriting`/`.allowsDeleting`/`.allowsAddingSubItems` (was `.allowsReading`-only, since the backend didn't exist until now).

Directory-only creation is accepted-but-not-persisted for this iteration (documented inline): `LocalChangeProcessor` has no directory-admission signal, so an empty folder exists on-disk but isn't durably recorded until a file lands inside it or a reconcile pass observes it -- same as an out-of-band `mkdir` on an Eager folder today.

## Review

Independent Codex pass (`codex exec -s read-only`) found and I fixed:
- **High**: content replacement used remove-then-move, opening a real window where the filesystem watcher could observe the destination absent and emit its own tombstone racing the explicit notify. Fixed with `FileManager.replaceItemAt` (atomic rename) when the destination exists.
- **Medium**: `deleteItem` bailed on `NSFileNoSuchFileError` -- exactly what a retry of an already-removed-but-never-notified delete looks like, stranding it un-admitted forever. Now falls through to notify on that specific error.
- **Medium**: `modifyItem` claimed every `changedFields` entry was applied even though only `.contents` is handled. Now returns the rest as `stillPendingFields`.

Two accepted gaps, documented inline rather than fixed: no rollback story for disk-mutated-then-notify-failed (self-heals on File Provider's own retry), and empty-directory durability (see above).

## Test plan
- [x] 4 new daemon-side tests exercising the full `LocalWriteRequest` → `process_event` path directly: create admits exactly one DAG change, a duplicate replay of unchanged content does not double-admit, delete tombstones, an unknown `local_path` fails closed
- [x] `cargo test -p yadorilink-daemon --lib` (762 tests), `--test shell_ipc` (9 existing integration tests, unaffected)
- [x] `cargo test`/clippy/fmt on `fileprovider-core` (5 existing tests, unaffected)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` workspace-wide
- [x] relevant boundary check scripts (daemon-application-dependencies, daemon-composition-root, materialization-journal, phase7d8-local-capture-boundary, phase1b-application-boundary)
- [x] Xcode compile gate, all 3 schemes, rerun after the review-round Swift fixes
- [ ] No live macOS device/Finder testing available in this environment -- static review + compile gate is the extent of verification for the Swift side
- [ ] CI fast

author: d-scott-code
body:
## What this is

Phase 0 of a low-maintenance system to fairly distribute CandyCo's 4-seat Delta Center box (~120 events/year: Jazz, Utah Mammoth, concerts) to employees — so **no seat goes to waste** and the benefit **spreads across as many people as possible**.

It deliberately reuses the pattern this repo already runs for the daily production report: plain data files + a small script + a static page on GitHub Pages, plus Outlook emails. Nothing new to host or maintain.

**Live board (after Pages builds):** `/candyco-production/ticket-lottery/`

## The model

- Everyone eligible gets **1 base entry**; extra entries are **earned** (recognition, safety, reliability), capped at 10× so no one dominates.
- A **weighted random draw** picks winners; **recent winners get a 45-day cooldown** (excluded from premium events, reduced odds on standard) — this is what spreads tickets around.
- Premium events cap parties at 2 (`max_party`) to serve two households; lower-demand events allow a full 4 so seats fill.
- Winners get 48h to confirm; unclaimed seats cascade down an ordered **waitlist**, then show as **last-minute open seats** anyone can grab.

## What's included

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ticket-lottery/draw.py` | Weighted lottery engine (stdlib only). Emits a privacy-safe public results file + a private details file for emails. |
| `ticket-lottery/index.html` | Employee board (open events, last-minute seats, recent draws) in CandyCo brand. Reads only `events.json` + `results.json` — no PII. |
| `ticket-lottery/data/` | Sample events / members / entries + generated results so it runs end-to-end today. |
| `ticket-lottery/emails/` | Outlook-safe `winner` / `entered` / `reminder` templates. |
| `ticket-lottery/README.md` | Pilot setup, the weekly loop, and HR/legal/tax guardrails. |
| `ticket-lottery/.gitignore` | Excludes `draw_details.json` so real emails never reach public Pages. |

## Verified

- `python3 draw.py --all --seed 42` runs reproducibly; premium events spread to 2 households, standard events fill, waitlist orders correctly, cooldown logic applied.
- All data files valid JSON; board rendered in headless Chromium (screenshot checked) — open events, live countdowns, a genuine last-minute-seats card, and privacy-safe winner chips.
- Public `results.json` contains only "First L." + dept — no names/emails.

## Before launch (in README checklist)

- Create the Microsoft Form + SharePoint list; set `FORM_URL` in `index.html`.
- Swap sample data for the real pilot roster/events.
- **HR/legal sign-off** on earning criteria (reward *leading* safety behaviors, not "no injuries"; don't penalize protected leave); **Finance** note on fringe-benefit tax.
- Decide board access: it's PII-free for public Pages, or move behind M365 auth if you'd rather it be internal-only.

Phase 1 (schedule the draw + auto-send emails + auto-cascade the waitlist) and Phase 2 (plants via QR/kiosk/SMS + AI helpers) follow.

author: paolaguevara2526
body:
## Qué pasó

Se liberó el insumo masivamente para el período `2026-08`, y los impuestos siguieron mostrando **«esperando»**.

No era un fallo del emparejamiento: los vencimientos en pantalla son **retenciones de julio** (período `2026-07`), que se declaran en agosto. El sistema busca —correctamente— la liberación de **`2026-07`**, que es el mes de los **datos**. Se liberó agosto; hacía falta julio.

Es el desfase de un mes que quedó decidido esta semana, apareciendo en la operación.

## El problema real

La columna decía **«esperando»** a secas. Sin nombrar el mes que falta, **quien libera el mes equivocado no tiene cómo darse cuenta**: liberó, la pantalla siguió igual, y no hay nada en la interfaz que explique por qué.

Ahora la celda muestra el período que falta —`⏳ esperando 2026-07`— y el tooltip aclara que es el mes de los datos, no el mes en que se trabaja.

## Lo que no cambia

El emparejamiento sigue igual, porque estaba bien. Esto es puramente hacer visible una causa que ya existía.

## Verificación

90 pruebas de API + 26 de web en verde; `build` limpio. Sin migración.

author: tommyzhang100504
body:
### What this PR does

**Before this PR:** the developer-mode call trace (`http.request` span) recorded the request body at span setup time — the serialized body the AI SDK produced *before* any provider-specific fetch wrapper ran. Providers that rewrite the body inside their fetch wrapper (DashScope `web_extractor`, Ark include-stripping, Codex/Grok body coercion) therefore showed a body in the trace panel that was **never sent**. Concretely, a DashScope Responses request displayed `tools: [web_search]` with `reasoning.effort: "none"` while the actual wire request carried `tools: [web_search, web_extractor]` and `enable_thinking: true` — and the server even rejected the one the trace claimed.

**After this PR:** `customFetch` (the innermost base fetch) records the final on-wire body into a `Symbol`-keyed slot attached to the `RequestInit`; `httpTraceFetch` reads that slot back once the request has been built and overwrites the span's `inputs` attribute. The trace now shows the body that actually went onto the wire, for any provider — current or future — that transforms the body on the way down the fetch chain.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The trace is a debugging aid that must reflect the request the server actually received; otherwise users copy a body from the trace, replay it, and get a different (often rejected) request. The response side was already accurate (it tees the real stream), so the distortion was one-sided: only the request body.

**The following tradeoffs were made:**

- The fix lives at the two ends of the fetch chain (`httpTraceFetch` at the outer span, `customFetch` at the innermost wire) rather than in each provider transform. This keeps a single mechanism instead of N per-provider patches, at the cost of a small module-level contract (a `Symbol` slot) that new body-rewriting providers must be aware of.
- The slot is a `Symbol`-keyed property on `RequestInit`, which survives the `{ ...init, body: transformed }` object spreads every provider transform uses — verified by test. When the slot is absent (no transform in the chain, or a non-spread path), `httpTraceFetch` is a strict no-op and keeps its original capture, so there is no behavior change for providers that don't rewrite the body.
- Bodies that are not strings (streams, `FormData`, `Blob`) are still skipped, matching the existing `readRequestBody` policy — the trace never breaks the real request.

**The following alternatives were considered:**

1. **Option A — have each provider transform wrapper write the corrected body back onto the span.** Rejected: it is inherently per-provider and easy to miss. Every existing wrapper (DashScope, Ark, Codex, Grok) would need its own patch, and any *future* body-rewriting wrapper would silently reintroduce the bug. It also couples provider code to the observability span, which is the wrong dependency direction.

2. **Option B — reorder assembly so the trace wraps the innermost fetch (below the provider transforms).** Rejected: the assembly order in `buildAgentParams.ts` / `config.ts` is load-bearing for several concerns (OAuth retry in `authenticatedFetch`, `customParamsFetch` layering, `??=` defaulting). Moving the trace inside would touch 6–8 assembly sites and carries high regression risk for a debugging aid, and any new wrapper stacked outside the trace would reintroduce the bug.

3. **Option C (chosen) — `customFetch` records the final body into a `Symbol` slot; the trace overwrites `inputs` from it.** The innermost fetch is the single point where the body is guaranteed to be the final wire body, so one mechanism captures every transform — current and future — with the smallest change surface (2 source files + tests). The symbol travels through all `{ ...init, body }` spreads automatically, and the mechanism degrades to a no-op when absent.

Links to places where the discussion took place: <!-- internal review of Options A/B/C by two independent reviewers; Option C recommended -->

### Breaking changes

None. The change only corrects what the developer-mode trace *shows*; no request behavior, wire format, or API surface changes.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- The trace is gated behind developer mode (`app.developer_mode.enabled`), so this is a debug-path-only change.
- `customFetch` is the repo-designated innermost base fetch (its docstring already states it "composes as the innermost layer"), which is why the slot write lives there rather than in a new wrapper.
- Provider transforms are all of the form `customFetch(input, { ...init, body: transform(init?.body) })`; the `Symbol` slot survives the spread by reference, so the trace reads the same slot object the innermost fetch wrote.
- Tests: new contract test in `httpTraceFetch.test.ts` (inner fetch rewrites body via the slot → span `inputs` reflects the post-transform body) and in `customFetch.test.ts` (slot receives the exact body sent to `net.fetch`). Existing 25 tests in these two files plus the wider `src/main/ai/**` suite (770+ tests) pass; `tsgo typecheck:node` and oxlint/biome are clean.

### Checklist

This checklist is not enforcing, but it's a reminder of items that could be relevant to every PR.
Approvers are expected to review this list.

- [x] Branch: This PR targets the correct branch — `main` for active development, `v1` for v1 maintenance fixes
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future contributors
- [x] Code: [Write code that humans can understand](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Martin_Fowler#code-for-humans) and [Keep it simple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle)
- [x] Refactor: You have [left the code cleaner than you found it (Boy Scout Rule)](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/97-things-every/9780596809515/ch08.html)
- [x] Upgrade: Impact of this change on upgrade flows was considered and addressed if required
- [ ] Documentation: A [user-guide update](https://docs.cherry-ai.com) was considered and is present (link) or not required. Check this only when the PR introduces or changes a user-facing feature or behavior.
- [x] Self-review: I have reviewed my own code (e.g., via [`/gh-pr-review`](/.claude/skills/gh-pr-review/SKILL.md), `gh pr diff`, or GitHub UI) before requesting review from others

### Release note

```release-note
Fixed the developer-mode call trace showing a request body that differs from what was actually sent to the provider (e.g. missing DashScope web_extractor / thinking settings). The trace now reflects the real on-wire request body.
```
