author: erick-otenyo
body:
Closes #31.

An open propagation gap outlives the evidence that would close it. Past the raw retention window the Global Broker rows that could settle it have been expired, so nothing can ever close it and nothing can ever find it again — and nothing retired it either, so the report filled with rows nobody can act on and nobody can clear. Every one of them genuine, which is what made it worse: last spring's gaps sitting permanently above this morning's is how a report stops being opened, which is the failure the reports exist to prevent.

## The decision

The issue left one question for triage: what an unclosable gap should be called. This takes the second of its two answers — **keep it, stop leading with it** — which reads truer to the model's own docstring, *"a gap not written down while its rows still exist is a finding that cannot be made again"*.

So the row is kept. It is the last thing that holds the UUID, since the rollups carry counts alone, so deleting it would destroy the only record of how that path behaved, and marking it closed would say the world carried a notification nobody knows the fate of. What it stops being is something to send somebody to a centre about.

**No new setting.** The issue sketched a horizon alongside `WIS2WATCH_PROPAGATION_WINDOW_HOURS`; this uses the raw retention cutoff itself. A second knob could only disagree with the first, and the disagreement would be either gaps reported that nothing can check or gaps withheld that something still can. It is named once — `evidence_horizon` — because the report has to print the instant it bounds itself at.

## What the tool now distinguishes

`PropagationGap.objects.within_evidence(now)` is a gap something could still settle either way; `beyond_evidence(now)` is one this tool merely stopped being able to check. Derived from the retention window rather than stamped on the row, so there is no migration and nothing to go stale when an installation changes how long it keeps messages.

The propagation report is bounded at that horizon — as long as the forensic window rather than as long as the installation has been running — and says what it left out: how many, and before when. A bound that goes unsaid is truncation. It is said above the empty state as well as above the table, because a report bounded to nothing would otherwise announce that everything published has reached the Global Broker, which is the one thing it does not know about the gaps past its horizon.

`GapReport` gains a `describe_bound`, so the four reports bounded by their filters rather than by truncation say nothing, and a sixth that has to truncate says so in the same place and the same way.

## What review changed

The second commit answers three findings, each covered by tests:

- **The digest read the bounded report and called the finding fixed.** A gap crossing the horizon is a permanent absence, and no grace period can rescue one that never ends. The clearing is not false — a centre leaves that way only when nothing new has gone missing there for the whole forensic window — but it is not the fix it reads as either. Each report's account of what it bounded is now carried into the mail beside its news, and the gaps that caused such a clearing are the very ones counted in it.
- **The index bounded its count without saying so.** That count is what decides whether a report is worth opening, so it says what it left out where it is read rather than on the page behind it.
- **The horizon was worked out twice**, once in the queryset and once for the sentence — exactly what the shared helper existed to prevent.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The digest still cannot tell "fixed" from "no longer checkable"** — it qualifies the news rather than distinguishing it. Making the distinction needs a fifth callable on `GapReport`, for one report's one case; filed as #33 rather than decided here.
- **Nothing retires the row.** `PropagationGap` rows past the horizon accumulate in the database as before, out of the reports. They are small, and they are the only thing left holding the UUIDs; if that ever needs bounding it is a retention question rather than a reporting one.
- **The evaluation window is untouched.** `evaluate_propagation` already clamped to the same cutoff; what changed is what the reports do with what it recorded.
- No migration.

846 tests pass.

author: ohioma-eboreime-p
body:
Fixes from an independent review of the merged S5 core loop. Every finding was re-verified against the actual code before fixing.

## Fixes

**1 · HIGH — failed upload permanently locks the user out + orphans storage** (`frontend/src/lib/sessions.js`)
`uploadSession` inserted the `pending` row (claiming the `(user_id, ld_sha256)` dedup slot) then uploaded files / inserted laps / flipped to `complete` — with **no cleanup** on failure. Since `listSessions` hides `pending` rows, any post-insert error left an invisible row that made every retry of that file fail with *"You already uploaded this exact session"* — permanently — plus orphaned Storage objects. **Worst case: it bricked a new account** whose demo seed half-failed. Now the post-insert work is wrapped so a failure **rolls back** (delete the row → cascade-drops laps; `storage.remove` the objects) and re-throws the original error; uploads use `{ upsert: true }` so a retry after a partial upload doesn't 409.

**2 · MED-HIGH — `Math.min/max(...samples)` crashes on real files** (`frontend/src/lib/ingest.js`)
Spreading a channel's samples throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` past ~100k elements — a real multi-lap/endurance export hits that on a single 50 Hz channel, crashing the whole upload. The committed fixture is truncated (300 samples), so the suite never caught it. Replaced all 4 sites with a single-pass `extent()`; added `ingest.extent.test.js` that proves the spread overflows at 500k where `extent()` doesn't.

**3 · MED — demo session polluted real Progression stats** (`frontend/src/components/ProgressionTab.jsx`)
The seeded `is_demo` session counted toward the driver's real gap / trend / best. Now excluded from Progression grouping (still shown in the Sessions list).

**4 · LOW — stale migration cross-reference** — `…12000000` → `…12030000`.

## Left documented, not fixed (low severity)
`valid` lap flag really means "has a following boundary" (mis-times out-laps); the `UNRELIABLE` badge path is currently dead code (empty set — consistent with the 10-Aug reclassification); `.ld` local wall-clock stored as UTC. Noted in the review for a later pass.

## Verified good (unchanged)
Tenant isolation (RLS on `auth.uid()`, no spoofable client `user_id`), the DB atomicity constraint + dedup, EMPTY flags genuinely **rendered** in `SessionDetail`, and disabled tabs honestly marked as scaffolding.

## Checks
32/32 Vitest, `oxlint`, and build green. Ring 3 (the gate merged in #4) will re-verify RLS/atomicity on this PR's CI.

author: chrreiter
body:
## Summary

The three follow-ups the V0.5.0 milestone still carried, plus the plan documents the
milestone's own exit criteria say to delete. Each commit stands alone and can be read on its
own; they are in one PR because they are the tail of one milestone and none is more than a
few dozen lines.

**`fix(ws): announce a location's own area change` — closes #419.** `location/update`
broadcast on the `locations` topic only when the request carried `new_parent_id` or `name`. A
request carrying just `area_id` re-anchors a whole subtree — every item under it gets a new
`effective_area_id` — and said nothing, so a second viewer filtered to the area the subtree
just left kept listing items that had left it. Confirmed live during H3, not inferred.

The action is now decided by what changed rather than by which keys arrived: a new parent or a
new area is `moved`, a new name alone is `renamed`, and a call that changes nothing announces
nothing. That settles the two things the presence-keyed shape got wrong and #419 folded into
its notes — the card's editor submits every field on every save, so a plain rename announced a
move, and a call changing both parent and name announced twice. Still no item events: the
items did not change, and a client tracking a filtered set re-lists on the `locations` event.
The card needs no change — `onLocationsEvent` already re-lists on `moved`.

**`perf(models): parse a filter's location ids once per query` — closes #425.**
`_item_matches_locations` rebuilt a `uuid.UUID` from the filter's constant ids inside the
per-item loop. The selection is now parsed once beside the date bounds, which are parsed there
for the same reason. Behaviour is identical, error case included: a selection that parses to
nothing still selects nothing rather than falling through to "no location filter", which is
what a single malformed id has always done — pinned by the early return and by the tests that
already covered it.

Per #425's own instruction, `filter_items` itself is left alone: its rank comes from thirteen
independent guarded predicates, and the prototype that flattens them measured slower.

**`fix(card): count locations before the import preview says nothing would change` — closes
#420.** The "nothing to do" hint counted items only, so a document that writes locations and
no items rendered `Nothing in this file would change the inventory` beside a count table
reading `LOCATIONS Add +4`. Both kinds now count towards the hint, and the execute button
names what it will write in the same terms — `Import 192 items · 6 locations`, either half
alone when only one applies, and a bare `Import` when the document writes nothing. The
added/updated split stays in the count tables directly above, which carry it for both kinds;
repeating it on the button would need four numbers.

**`docs(dev): retire the V0.5.0 plan and its handovers.`** Both documents describe finished
work, and the plan's §8 says to delete them in the PR that closes the last issue. This is it.

### Milestone state

All eighteen V0.5.0 issues are resolved. #200 was closed by hand as **not planned** — its
premise did not survive H8's measurement, and a `Closes` reference would have closed it as
completed, which is the wrong state. Its reopen trigger (~5 000 items) is recorded on the
issue.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that changes existing behavior)
- [x] Documentation / tooling / CI
- [ ] Refactor (no functional change)

`location/update`'s event is a contract change in the narrow sense that fewer events are
emitted for a call carrying both a new parent and a new name. Nothing in the card or the
documented client behaviour distinguishes them: both re-list.

## How was this tested?

- [x] Backend: `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 uv run pytest -q` (916 passed, 22 skipped),
      `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run mypy` — all green.
- [x] Frontend (`cards/haventory-card`): `npx eslint .`, `npm run typecheck`,
      `npx vitest run` (1812 passed), `npm run build` — all green.

New coverage — backend: reassigning a location's own `area_id` delivers exactly one
`locations` `moved` event and no item events, to a connection holding both an `items` and a
`locations` subscription; a rename carrying an unchanged `new_parent_id` is announced as
`renamed`; a call changing parent and area at once is one `moved`; a call that changes nothing
announces nothing. A location-filtered query parses each selected id exactly once whatever the
item count, counted rather than benchmarked.

Frontend: a locations-only document draws no "nothing would change" hint; the button names
only the kind a document actually writes, and reads a bare `Import` when it writes neither.

`scripts/test_integration.sh` was **not** run: this environment's uv can reach no Python 3.14
build past `3.14.0rc2`, which `homeassistant==2026.6.0` refuses (`requires_python >=3.14.2`).
That is #433, filed from this session. Nothing in this diff touches a command schema, which is
the half the phacc mode is the only place to observe.

## Live verification

Two of the three are worth a look on the dev instance; neither gates the review.

- **#419** — the H3 step-8 scenario that found it, run again: two tabs on `/haventory`, tab A
  filtered to an area, then reassign that location's own area in the location editor. Tab A
  must re-list on its own and drop the departed items, where before it kept showing them.
  Watch that a plain rename now announces `renamed` and that a no-op save announces nothing —
  devtools WS frames are where both are visible.
- **#420** — export a backup, delete and hand-rebuild the locations, then preview that backup
  back: the preview must not say nothing would change, and the button must read
  `Import N locations`. The clean round trip on an untouched inventory is the negative case.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
- [x] Tests added/updated (happy path + at least one edge/error case).
- [x] Docs updated where behavior changed (`docs/backend_api_contract.md`,
      `docs/data_shapes.md` — the `location/update` event rule and what `moved` covers).
- [x] WebSocket API changes keep `ws.py`, `docs/backend_api_contract.md`, and
      `docs/data_shapes.md` in sync.
- [x] Essential invariants preserved (case-insensitive search, denormalized `location_path`,
      optimistic `version`). An area reassignment still touches no item's `version` or
      `updated_at`.
- [x] No file under `custom_components/haventory/` deleted or renamed, so `RETIRED_PATHS` is
      unchanged.

## Follow-ups

- #433, filed from this session: `requires-python = ">=3.14"` admits an interpreter Home
  Assistant refuses, and the failure surfaces as an unsatisfiable resolution rather than as a
  too-old interpreter. Two earlier V0.5.0 PRs flagged it in their own follow-up notes and
  neither filed it.
- #426, #430, #431 and #432 came out of the milestone's live runs and carry no milestone.
  They are real and none of them is in this diff.

Closes #419
Closes #420
Closes #425

author: timharris707
body:
Closes #175. Closes #176.

## What

The 2026-08-12 burn comparison (post-#169) showed total orchestration burn down ~68%, with the biggest remaining driver being orchestrator context accumulation mid/late run: everything the orchestrator ingests is re-read at every subsequent wake, so ingestion compounds. Two rules shrink what accumulates:

- **#175 — compact lane-report contract.** §5 step 1: the close-out audit reads the lane's diff in the lane's workspace at the scope the item names, never wholesale into the orchestrator's context; oversized diffs go to a delegated verifier (§7 slot) that reads in full and reports compactly. The lane-brief template's output contract now asks for diff stat + per-command exit codes + load-bearing hunks only, never full diffs or transcripts.
- **#176 — lean wakes.** §1 item 5: a metronome wake is a minimal turn — re-arm, one small filtered check, a one-line status; broad ingestion waits for an event that needs it. The metronome keeps the cache warm; lean wakes keep the thing being cached from growing.

Plus two CHANGELOG entries.

## Verification

Re-run by the orchestrator in the lane's worktree: `check_router_freshness.py`, `check_invocation_freshness.py`, `check_site_disclosure.py`, `git diff --check` — all exit 0; diff touches only the three intended files. Doc-only change, no visual surface.

author: anoziere
body:
Refs #1664.

## Symptom

Postage can only be taxed with the one tax rule configured shop-wide. `AbstractDeliveryModuleWithState::buildOrderPostage()` (core/lib/Thelia/Module/AbstractDeliveryModuleWithState.php:66 before this change) read `taxrule_id_delivery_module` and nothing else, so every carrier in the shop was forced onto the same rate.

The method already accepted an explicit `$taxRuleId` fourth argument, and most bundled carriers use it — each one re-implementing its own setting, its own back-office controller and its own form:

- `ColissimoHomeDelivery.php:285`, `ColissimoPickupPoint.php:267`
- `ChronopostHomeDelivery.php:388`, `ChronopostPickupPoint.php:382`
- `MondialRelayHomeDelivery.php:392`, `MondialRelayPickupPoint.php:372`
- `DpdClassic.php:201`, `CustomDelivery.php:287`

A module that does not do this — `LocalPickup.php:65` calls `buildOrderPostage()` with three arguments — has no way to pick a rate at all.

## Change

The postage builder moves into `Thelia\Module\OrderPostageBuilderTrait`, which resolves the tax rule in three steps:

1. the id the module passes explicitly to `buildOrderPostage()`;
2. the module's own `postage_tax_rule_id` entry in `module_config`;
3. the shop-wide `taxrule_id_delivery_module`.

Step 2 is new; steps 1 and 3 behave exactly as before, so a carrier that already passes its own rule is unaffected. The setting lives in the existing `module_config` table, so there is no schema change.

`AbstractDeliveryModule` — the stateless base, which had no postage builder at all — now uses the same trait. `buildOrderPostage()` keeps its original signature, and no module in the ecosystem overrides it.

`getPostageTaxRuleId()` is exposed so a back-office screen can show which rule a given delivery module will actually apply.

## Scope

This makes the per-carrier choice first-class. It does not split postage VAT across a cart that mixes rates: the EU rule apportions the shipping charge over the goods pro rata their net values, which needs a per-rate breakdown next to `order.postage_tax` and therefore a new table. That design is written up on the issue.

## Verifying

`tests/Integration/Module/DeliveryModulePostageTaxRuleTest.php` covers the four branches: shop-wide rule with no module setting, module setting overriding it, explicit argument still winning over the module setting, and untaxed postage when nothing is configured.

Checked red before green: with the `module_config` lookup removed, `testModuleSettingOverridesTheShopWideRule` fails with `'VAT 20'` where `'VAT 5.5'` is expected.

author: officialinspire
body:
## Summary

Audited `updateBallPhysics()`'s anti-stuck detection (speed < `STUCK_SPEED_THRESHOLD_MS` for `STUCK_TIME_THRESHOLD_MS`) against nine scenarios: resting against a wall, rolling slowly downhill, near a flipper, between posts, sitting briefly in a guide, near the plunger, right after a soft collision, held by the Vision Gate, and during bonus/drain/reset transitions.

## Methodology note

This sandbox's headless rendering runs far slower than a real device (~2.7fps measured directly, vs. ~60fps), which makes observing the timer via the live render loop unreliable on its own — a single frame's `deltaMs` can itself approach or exceed `STUCK_TIME_THRESHOLD_MS`, aliasing against real physics jitter in a way that varies run to run. Verified instead by calling the exact detection algorithm directly at a controlled, realistic 60fps cadence (16.67ms steps) against real Havok-measured velocities, then independently confirmed the real render-loop path fires (or doesn't) the same way live.

## The false positive

A ball resting on the plunger (charging or just waiting for launch input) has near-zero velocity just like any other settled ball, and reaches `STUCK_TIME_THRESHOLD_MS` in under half a second — well inside normal player reaction time, meaning **every ordinary launch could route through an unwanted "rescue" kick**. The same `ballInPlay=false` window also covers wherever the ball lands after a real drain, before `resetBallToPlunger()` runs.

Every other scenario tested (resting against a wall, flipper, or bumper; wedged between posts; sitting in a lane channel; rolling slowly downhill) never produced a false trigger on its own: the table's 6.5-degree tilt keeps a genuinely free ball moving above `STUCK_SPEED_THRESHOLD_MS` within milliseconds unless something is actually blocking it — exactly the state this mechanism exists to catch. Vision Gate holds were already correctly guarded via the same pattern this fix extends.

## Fix

Gated `updateBallPhysics(mainBall, ...)` on `ballInPlay`, alongside the existing `visionGate.active` guard, with a defensive reset of `stuckTimeMs` for the skipped window (same unconditional-reset idiom `resetBallToPlunger()` already uses elsewhere). No change to the detection algorithm itself, the threshold constants, or any other call site — per the audit's own instruction, `STUCK_TIME_THRESHOLD_MS` was not touched.

- [x] Live end-to-end verification: a ball resting on the plunger for a full real-world 3 seconds no longer gets kicked (previously fired reliably under ~450ms)

author: cto-new[bot]
body:
## What

Migration **036 — Trust & Safety** for the Supabase database (owner applies manually via SQL Editor, 033/034/035 precedent), delivered in two places:

- `supabase/migrations/036_trust_safety.sql` (new per-migration file, repo convention)
- `supabase/run-me-in-sql-editor.sql` (same block appended, byte-identical — copy-paste friendly for the owner)

Plus one small server-side caller fix in `src/lib/notifications/actions.ts` required for F2 to be safe (see F2 below).

**No migrations were run and nothing was executed against the live database — this PR is the deliverable for the owner to apply.**

## Why

Sprint 8 (Safety, Trust, Privacy & Relationship Decision Support) audit findings from `S8_AUDIT.md` §C:

- **F2 (HIGH)** — `create_notification_for_user` RPC (migration 020) is SECURITY DEFINER and was granted to `authenticated`, so *any signed-in user* could write a notification row for *any target user id* (spam/annoyance vector).
- **F3 (HIGH)** — `comparison_reports` INSERT policy (migration 010) is `WITH CHECK (true)`, so *any signed-in user* could insert a report row for *any pairing_id*.
- Owner brief §7 requires **blocking to be database-enforced, not UI-only** ("no new invitations, no new connections, no access") and §8 requires a `reports` table; the owner picked the **own-table option** for `shared_agreements` (candidate B).

## Each block, in plain language

1. **`shared_agreements`** — new table for agreed relationship decisions, modeled 1:1 on `shared_goals` (migration 035): columns, indexes, `updated_at` trigger, and the same four participant RLS policies (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE via `EXISTS` on pairings; INSERT also enforces `created_by = auth.uid()`).
2. **`blocked_users`** — user blocks another user. UNIQUE(blocker, blocked), CHECK cannot block yourself. RLS: users manage only their own block list (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE own rows, no UPDATE).
3. **`pairing_is_blocked(uuid)`** — SECURITY DEFINER helper (same pattern as `get_profile_display_name`, migration 025). Returns only a boolean: whether a block exists between a pairing's two participants in *either* direction. SECURITY DEFINER is required because `blocked_users` RLS only lets a user read their *own* blocking rows — an inline policy subquery could never see the "the other user blocked me" direction.
4. **`reports`** — abuse/safety reports (harassment/inappropriate/unsafe/privacy/ai/other + optional description). `reported_user_id` is nullable (some reports are about AI output, not a user); `connection_id` is ON DELETE SET NULL so the report survives a disconnect (evidence preservation). RLS: reporter reads/inserts their own reports only; **no UPDATE/DELETE policies** — status changes (open → reviewed/actioned/dismissed) are service-role only. No public feed.
5. **F2 fix** — `REVOKE EXECUTE` on `create_notification_for_user` from `authenticated, anon`; `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role`. ⚠️ **Caller fix included**: the task's assumption that "all web server-side callers use the service client" is *not* true — `createNotification()` in `src/lib/notifications/actions.ts` called the RPC via the **session client** for cross-user notifications (live flows: pairing accept notification, connection request/accept notifications). Without a fix, applying this migration would break those web flows. `createNotification` now uses the service client for the cross-user RPC (mirrors `mobile-api.ts notifyInviteAccepted()`; tests updated/verified — `notifications.test.ts` 8/8 pass, `tsc` clean). The service-role grant keeps the service-client callers (mobile API accept route) working.
6. **F3 fix** — drops the comparison_reports INSERT policy under both historical names (010 `"Service inserts comparison reports"` and the 024 rename `"Partners can insert own report"`), recreates it as a participant-checked insert mirroring the SELECT policy expression verbatim. The web refresh/accept route writes via the service client (bypasses RLS) and the mobile app never inserts comparison_reports, so tightening is safe.
7. **Blocked-relationship enforcement** — `ALTER POLICY` on the pairings SELECT/UPDATE policies and the pairing_invitations SELECT/UPDATE policies: the existing participant/inviter check now also requires `NOT pairing_is_blocked(...)`. The 025 anon policy is untouched (see below). Downstream tables (`comparison_reports`, `relationship_topics`, `shared_goals`, `shared_agreements`, `pairing_messages`) grant access via `EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pairings ...)`, and those subqueries read pairings under its RLS — so a blocked user's subquery returns no rows and the downstream rows become invisible **automatically**. No per-table changes needed (verified against the policy texts in 008/010/011/034/035).

## How the owner applies

1. Open the Supabase SQL Editor for the project.
2. Paste the appended `MIGRATION 036` block from `supabase/run-me-in-sql-editor.sql` (or the whole file) and run it.
3. Alternatively, run `supabase/migrations/036_trust_safety.sql` directly (identical content).
4. The block is additive except the three authorized fixes (F2 revoke, F3 policy replacement, narrowed pairings/invitations policies). No tables dropped, no data deleted, Blueprint tables/scoring untouched.

## What was deliberately NOT changed

- **Migration-025 anon policy `"Anyone can read pending pairing by code"`** — untouched. Audit F1 (anyone holding the 8-char code can read a pending pairing's embedded Blueprint snapshot) is **disclose-only this sprint** per the audit recommendation; narrowing it is a future owner-ratified web change. Note: a *pending* pairing (invitee_user_id still NULL) can't have a block yet, so the block check only applies once both participants exist on the row (accepted/completed).
- `pairings` has **no DELETE policy** (unchanged; disconnect stays server-side via the mobile API routes).
- `comparison_reports` UPDATE and SELECT policies — unchanged (already participant-checked).
- `connection_requests` (027) is a separate from/to table not linked to pairings and does **not** inherit the blocked invisibility — blocking enforcement there (and in the service-client accept/refresh routes, which bypass RLS) is a suggested S8-b follow-up at the server layer.

## Files

- `supabase/migrations/036_trust_safety.sql` (new)
- `supabase/run-me-in-sql-editor.sql` (appended block)
- `src/lib/notifications/actions.ts` (F2 caller fix: service client for cross-user notification RPC)

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `bun test src/lib/__tests__/notifications.test.ts` — 8/8 pass (incl. "creates a notification for another user via RPC")
- `bun test src/lib/__tests__/pairings-flow.test.ts` — 12/12 pass
- No DB queries/executions performed (SQL deliverable only)

## Summary
Grace demonstrated live that ReciMe successfully imports a full recipe from an Instagram share in seconds — falsifying this session's prior "confirmed industry-wide, no competitor can" conclusion (which was desk research, not a live test).

Re-investigation confirms Meta's oEmbed API path really is dead (caption field deleted from the schema in 2020, three first-party Meta sources). But ReciMe's own docs say import requires the **native iOS share sheet from inside the Instagram app** — the same mechanism Sloe already uses — and reads the caption as its first-tier method. Sloe's own code has a 2026-04-30 doc comment claiming Instagram's share sheet supplies caption text, but this has never been empirically verified on a real device.

This adds a one-shot diagnostic PostHog event (`debug_share_intent_raw_captured`) that fires before any filtering, capturing the raw `expo-share-intent` payload (`type`, `files`, `webUrl`, `text`, `meta`). Verified the native `expo-share-intent` Share Extension template is a clean, non-lossy pass-through, so if Instagram does supply distinct caption text, it'll show up here — and the existing forwarding logic in `_layout.tsx` already handles it correctly with zero further code change needed.

**Remove this event + call site once the live test settles the question** — see the event's doc comment in `src/lib/analytics/events.ts`.

## Test plan
- [x] Mobile typecheck — clean
- [x] Mobile lint (scoped) — 0 new errors/warnings
- [x] Mobile unit suite — 5732 passed
- [x] `tests/unit/analyticsEvents.test.ts` — 29 passed
- [ ] Live device test: Grace shares a real Instagram post to Sloe via the native share sheet, we read back the PostHog event

author: eas-yin
body:
## 자기소개
안녕하세요, 병웅 님! 이번 미션을 통해 Spring을 처음 학습하고 있는 이지인입니다.
처음 학습하는 만큼 학습 테스트의 이해도 오래 걸리고, 미션을 수행하는 데도 꽤 헷갈렸습니다.
제가 어떤 생각으로 구현했는지 간단한 설명과 질문도 함께 드리겠습니다.
리뷰 정말 감사합니다!


## 구현 과정
### 1단계
학습 테스트를 참고하여 웹 요청을 처리하는 데 필요한 Spring Web 의존성과 HTML 템플릿을 사용하기 위한 Thymeleaf 의존성을 추가했습니다.
이후 HomeController를 생성하고, / 요청 시 home.html을 반환하도록 구현했습니다.
처음에는 @GetMapping('localhost:8080')처럼 작성해야 한다고 생각했습니다. 지금까지 학습 테스트나 앞의 설명에서 봤을 때는 항상 /home 이런 느낌이어서 헷갈렸습니다. 학습 테스트를 진행하며 localhost:8080은 호스트이고 @GetMapping에는 경로를 작성한다는 것을 이해했습니다.

### 2단계
/reservation 요청 시 reservation.html을 반환하도록 구현했습니다.
그리고 예약 목록 조회를 위해 예약 번호, 예약자 이름, 날짜, 시간을 가지는 Reservation 클래스를 만들었습니다. 이후 학습 테스트에서 구현했던 read() 메서드를 참고하여 /reservations 요청 시 ResponseEntity<List<Reservation>>를 반환하도록 구현했습니다.


## AI를 활용해 학습한 내용
2단계 테스트의 .body("size()", is(3)) 코드를 처음 보았을 때 is(3)의 의미를 알지 못해 AI를 통해 확인했습니다.
이를 통해 is(3)은 /reservations 요청으로 반환된 예약 목록에 3개의 데이터가 있는지 검증한다는 것을 학습했습니다.


## 궁금한 점
### 1. @ResponseBody와 ResponseEntity의 차이가 궁금합니다.
학습 테스트에서 json() 메서드는 @ResponseBody를 사용해 객체를 반환했고, read() 메서드는 ResponseEntity를 사용해 객체 목록을 반환했습니다.
두 방식 모두 결과적으로 페이지에서 JSON 형식으로 응답되는 것을 확인했는데, 그렇다면 두 방식은 어떤 차이가 있는지 궁금합니다. 또한 실제로 사용할 때는 어떤 기준으로 @ResponseBody와 ResponseEntity를 선택하는지도 궁금합니다.

### 2. README의 기능 목록은 어느 시점에 작성하는 것이 좋은지 궁금합니다.
이번 미션에서는 코드를 모두 구현한 뒤 마지막에 README를 작성했습니다.
미션을 진행할 때 README의 기능 목록을 코드 구현과 함께 작성해 나가는 것이 좋은지, 아니면 모든 구현을 마친 뒤 마지막에 정리해서 작성하는 것이 좋은지 궁금합니다.

## 마무리
Spring을 처음 학습하며 진행한 미션이라 아직 부족하거나 잘못 이해한 부분이 있을 수 있습니다.
이번 리뷰를 통해 제가 놓친 부분이나 더 고민해 보면 좋을 부분이 있다면 편하게 말씀해 주시면 감사하겠습니다!
리뷰해 주셔서 감사합니다. 😊

author: orestjge
body:
## 何を直すか

mp4 などのサムネイルもスクロール中にちらつく。#121 と**同じ形のバグ**で、`post_images.dart` の 3 箇所（レスのサムネ・ニコニコのサムネ・ビューアの送り先に敷くフレーム）が残っていた。

`FutureBuilder` は**完了済みの Future でも最初の 1 フレームは「まだ無い」を返す**ので、画面外へ出た行が戻ってくるたびに `frame: null`＝無地の再生カードから出し直していた。

**こちらは箱の形まで戻るので、リンクカードより目立つ。** カードはフレームのヘッダから読んだ縦横比で組んでいるため、無地の 1 フレームだけ縦横比が失われて正方形になり、**下のレス全部が動く**。

## どうしたか

### もう作ってあるフレームは待たずに敷く

| | 控え | 待たずに引く口 |
|---|---|---|
| `VideoThumbnails` | `_resolved`（追加） | `cached(url)`（追加） |
| `NicoThumbnails` | `_resolved`（追加） | `cached(id)`（追加） |

呼び出し側は先に `cached()` を見て、あればそれで組む。無いときだけ従来どおり `resolve()` + `FutureBuilder` に回す。#121 の `LinkCard` と同じ形に揃えた。

### あわせて、失敗を覚えるようにする

これまで失敗（null）はキャッシュから消していた（「次回再試行できるよう」）。ところが `resolve` は `build` から呼ばれる——**スクロール中は毎フレーム通る**——ので、サムネを取れない動画が 1 本あると、そのつど OS のデコーダ（Android: MediaMetadataRetriever / iOS・macOS: AVAssetImageGenerator）を叩き直していた。ニコニコ側も同じで、getthumbinfo を毎フレーム叩いていた。

リンクプレビューと同じ「失敗も覚える」に倒す。つっかえの一因としても効いていたはず。

**代わりに、一度失敗した動画はアプリを開き直すまで再挑戦しない。** 通信の一時的な不調で落ちたぶんも無サムネのままになる。そこが気になるなら、時間を置いての再挑戦（クールダウン）に変えられるので言ってください。

## テスト

`flutter test` 699 件 green、`flutter analyze` も No issues。

- **作り直しても、生成済みのサムネイルは無地に戻らない**（`post_images_test.dart`）— 敷いてから画面外へ出して State を捨て、作り直した**1 フレーム目**で、絵が出ていること・**箱が映像の形のまま**（正方形に戻らない）こと・生成し直していないことまで見る
- **失敗も覚えて、叩き直さない** — 動画とニコニコの両方。3 回 `resolve` して生成 1 回
- **生成済みのフレームは cached で待たずに引ける** — 動画とニコニコの両方

既存の `失敗（null）はキャッシュせず次回再試行する` は、今回の意図と正面から反対なので `失敗も覚えて、叩き直さない` に書き換えた。

author: einarjohnlagera
body:
Items 1 and 6 of `v0.74.0`. Frontend only — PR #1055 already shipped every piece of data this needs.

## What shipped

- **The Quiz tab stays visible, clickable and keyboard reachable while locked** — it carries a lock icon and an `aria-label` of "Quiz, locked" rather than being `disabled`. A tab that silently vanishes and later reappears reads as a glitch, and a learner cannot feel they unlocked something they never knew existed.
- **`PracticeQuizCard` is not mounted while locked** — not hidden behind CSS. The answers are in the client payload either way, so rendering them into the DOM would make the lock theatre.
- **The panel names the real condition using the pack's own question count** — `Score 3/3 on Quick Review to unlock` — with length-agnostic copy when the count is unavailable. No hardcoded `5`, because Quick Review administers whatever is in the stored row.
- **Curator exemption** via a shared `isQuizMasteryLockBypassed` predicate rather than an inline profile check.
- **`STUDY_PACK_QUIZ_TAB_OPENED_AFTER_UNLOCK`** fires once per tab open, only for unlocked non-curators.
- **An absent `quizMastered` is treated as locked**, matching the backend's fail-closed resolution.

## Copy fix caught during audit (`c8e2605b`)

The panel originally read *"Use **Redo Mistakes** to retry the ones you missed"*. **That label exists nowhere in the product** — the real button on the Quick Review results screen is **`Retry Incorrect Questions`**, and Challenge Quiz's similar-sounding action is `Redo Missed Questions`. A 4/5 learner would have gone hunting for a control that isn't there, which is the same stranded-learner failure the copy rewrite existed to fix. "Redo Mistakes" came from the `v0.74.0` brief and is planning vocabulary only; both feature docs now say it must never reach learner-facing copy.

## Scope boundary, deliberate

The lock covers **private Note Detail only**. The public share page (`/p/[token]`) and the generation-results view still reveal saved answers — gating the share page would lock it for anonymous viewers and break sharing outright. Recorded as accepted exceptions in `docs/features/quiz.md`, consistent with this being a UX progression affordance rather than a security boundary.

## Also included

One docs commit (`fb8a9686`) scoping the separate raw-LaTeX rendering fix into this release, with the production sizing that led to dropping its admin-backfill part. Same release, unrelated to the lock.

## Verification

1796 frontend tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint clean (20 pre-existing warnings, none from this diff).

Coverage includes: locked tab reachable with answers absent from the DOM; length-agnostic copy at `quizCount` 0/undefined; unlock event firing once per open and again on a genuine re-open; teacher **and** admin curators viewing the quiz without emitting unlock analytics; empty quizzes keeping their existing state.

body:
Gateway DB Extraction program, wave **W0**. Plan of record: `jeeb/PLAN-gateway-db-extraction-2026-08-12.md`.

## 1. Checklist item + PLAN clause

**W0-11** (the G-08 third, plus the G-18 retention half):

> "Install the W0 CI gates: **G-08 roster manifest (build fails if a deleted store interface remains on `StoreDurabilityGuard.Critical`; roster edit same-PR)**, G-22 one-way flag containment (repo ⊆ approved-flags registry), and the G-28 vocabulary lint on every fleet.json `generic:true` repo; **keep the migration double-apply gate**." (refs R1, F9)

G-22 ships in the sibling PR `gwdbx/w0-flag-registry`; the G-28 vocabulary lint is a different-repo item and is not in scope here.

PLAN clause — §5 riders:

> "**R1 guard-roster** same-PR rule + manifest CI check (G-08). **R2 backfills** = idempotent HTTP ingest only. **R6/R7** unchanged (device proofs; notification-service never a target)."

## 2. What ships

* `scripts/guard-roster.txt` — the roster manifest, generated from `StoreDurabilityGuard.cs`: 37 lines = `Critical` (33) + `KnownInMemoryBacklog` (1) + `UpstreamContractIncomplete` (1) + `IntentionalInMemory` (2), each `<Roster> <Iface> -> <Impl>[, <Impl>]`.
* `scripts/check-guard-roster.sh` — the gate (4 invariants), plus `--write` to regenerate the manifest.
* `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `guard-roster-gate` job. No existing job touched.

Design note: the **C# roster stays the source of truth** and the `.txt` is generated + drift-checked. Making DI read a text file at runtime would weaken the fail-closed boot guard, which is the thing G-08 exists to protect.

Second commit (`763ac3b`, review point P2) adds invariant **(0)**, which makes the gate un-neuterable: a parser regression that silently empties a roster would otherwise let `--write` bake the collapse into the manifest and the gate would pass on an empty world.

## 3. Guardrails enforced

**G-08 — "Guard roster edited in the same PR (R1)"**

> **rule**: Every step-5 store deletion edits the `StoreDurabilityGuard` critical roster in the SAME PR; no deleted interface may remain on the roster.
> **protects**: Prod availability: deleting a store without editing `StoreDurabilityGuard.Critical` fail-closes gateway boot (503).
> **enforcement**: Keep a roster manifest (`guard-roster.txt`, one interface per line) that `StoreDurabilityGuard.Critical` is built from; CI: `while read i; do git grep -q "interface $i" src/ || { echo "roster orphan: $i"; exit 1; }; done < guard-roster.txt` — plus review-rule: any PR deleting a store interface edits `guard-roster.txt` in the SAME PR.

**G-18 — "DROP migrations table-scoped, idempotent" (retention half only)**

> **enforcement**: Existing CI job 'Database migrations (idempotency + seed)' in `build.yml` runs `db/apply.sh` twice — the second pass must no-op …

This PR does not add or change any migration; invariant (3) only asserts that the existing double-apply/seed gate in `build.yml` is still present, so no later PR can quietly delete it.

Guardrail audit — literal output of `bash scripts/check-guard-roster.sh` at this branch head:

```
== G-08 gate: StoreDurabilityGuard roster manifest ==
-- (0) SHAPE: generator still sees all four rosters
OK: four rosters non-empty, Critical=33 (floor 25).
-- (1) DRIFT: scripts/guard-roster.txt vs StoreDurabilityGuard.cs
OK: manifest matches the four rosters (37 entries).
-- (2) ORPHAN: every manifest type is still declared under src/JeebGateway
OK: all manifest types are still declared.
-- (3) G-18: build.yml keeps the migration double-apply gate
OK: double-apply gate intact (apply=2 seed=2).

G-08 gate PASSED — roster manifest in sync, no orphans, double-apply gate intact.
```

exit status `0`.

## 4. Acceptance tests

Every negative test perturbs a clean tree, runs the gate, and reverts; `git status --porcelain` was empty afterwards in each case.

**N1 — a store removed from `StoreDurabilityGuard.Critical` without editing the manifest (invariant 1, the R1 same-PR rule).** Deleted the `ITiersStore` roster line from `StoreDurabilityGuard.cs`:

```
== G-08 gate: StoreDurabilityGuard roster manifest ==
-- (0) SHAPE: generator still sees all four rosters
OK: four rosters non-empty, Critical=32 (floor 25).
-- (1) DRIFT: scripts/guard-roster.txt vs StoreDurabilityGuard.cs
FAIL: guard-roster.txt has drifted from StoreDurabilityGuard.cs.
      The roster edit and the manifest MUST ship in the SAME PR as the
      store change (R1 / G-08) — a deleted store left on Critical
      fail-closes production boot with a 503. Regenerate with:
        scripts/check-guard-roster.sh --write
  --- scripts/guard-roster.txt
  +++ (generated)
  @@ -20,7 +20,6 @@
  ...
```

exit `1`, with the full unified diff of the drift printed.

**N2 — the exact G-08 failure mode: a store interface deleted from `src/` but LEFT on the roster (invariant 2).** Renamed the sole declaration of `ICmsSurfaceStore` so the type no longer exists:

```
== G-08 gate: StoreDurabilityGuard roster manifest ==
-- (0) SHAPE: generator still sees all four rosters
OK: four rosters non-empty, Critical=33 (floor 25).
-- (1) DRIFT: scripts/guard-roster.txt vs StoreDurabilityGuard.cs
OK: manifest matches the four rosters (37 entries).
-- (2) ORPHAN: every manifest type is still declared under src/JeebGateway
FAIL: roster orphan: JeebGateway.Cms.ICmsSurfaceStore (Critical) is on the manifest but no longer
      declared under src/JeebGateway — delete its roster line in this PR.
-- (3) G-18: build.yml keeps the migration double-apply gate
OK: double-apply gate intact (apply=2 seed=2).

G-08 gate FAILED — roster manifest is not trustworthy. See guardrails G-08/G-18.
```

exit `1`. This is precisely the 503-on-boot scenario G-08 protects against, caught at CI time.

**N3 — the G-18 double-apply gate removed from `build.yml` (invariant 3).** Changed one of the two `run: ./db/apply.sh` steps:

```
-- (3) G-18: build.yml keeps the migration double-apply gate
FAIL: .github/workflows/build.yml must run ./db/apply.sh and ./db/seed.sh TWICE
      (second pass must no-op) — found apply=1 seed=2. G-18.

G-08 gate FAILED — roster manifest is not trustworthy. See guardrails G-08/G-18.
```

exit `1`.

**N0 — the un-neuterable test (invariant 0, review point P2).** Simulated a parser regression by restyling a roster declaration so the generator no longer sees it. The gate fails **and `--write` refuses to regenerate**, so the collapse cannot be baked into the manifest:

```
== G-08 gate: StoreDurabilityGuard roster manifest ==
-- (0) SHAPE: generator still sees all four rosters
FAIL: generator emitted 0 entries for roster 'IntentionalInMemory' — it no longer parses
      its declaration in src/JeebGateway/Infrastructure/StoreDurabilityGuard.cs. Fix the generator; do NOT
      regenerate the manifest, that neuters the G-08 gate. (invariant 0)
```

`scripts/check-guard-roster.sh --write` on the same tree prints the identical FAIL and writes nothing. Both exit `1`. The `Critical` floor (`CRITICAL_MIN=25`, against 33 today) catches the same class of regression when a roster shrinks implausibly rather than to zero; a genuine shrink past the floor must lower it in the same PR.

## 5. No runtime behaviour change

This diff adds two files under `scripts/` and one CI job. It contains **no C# change and no configuration change**; `StoreDurabilityGuard.cs` is read-only input to the generator and is not modified. Nothing in this PR executes in the gateway process. Runtime behaviour at `66a7b9d` is bit-identical.

## 6. Pre-existing repo state (not caused by this diff)

At the base commit `origin/main` **`66a7b9d`** itself, two repo-level check scripts already fail — reproduced in a clean detached worktree of `66a7b9d`, i.e. with **zero** of this branch's changes present:

```
$ bash scripts/check-stateless-gateway.sh
...
R9 gate FAILED — gateway is not stateless. See ADR-001-rev2.
$ echo $?
1
```

author: taras
body:
Closes #453.

## Why

A document that never wrote `<Output>` printed an uncaught failure into its own
text and exited 0. A failed step could therefore be followed by a publish, and
`xmd run` reported success for a run that had gone wrong. `<Output>` was the only
thing that made a failure count — which put the decision "did this run fail" in
the hands of a construct whose job is choosing what renders.

## What changes

Before:

```md
Checking the build.

```sh exec
./scripts/build.sh    # exits 3
```

Publishing.
```

`Publishing.` rendered, an `<!-- ERROR ... -->` comment sat between the two, and
the command exited 0.

After: the run stops at the failing block. `Checking the build.` is still on
stdout, the diagnostic is on stderr once, `Publishing.` never renders, and
`xmd run` exits 1. Replay returns the same determined failure without repeating
any effect.

Printing and continuing is still available — it is now asked for:

```md
<PrintErrors>

```sh exec
./scripts/optional-check.sh
```

</PrintErrors>

Publishing.
```

## How it works

```text
execute() → documentWorkflow → ErrorMode.set("output") for a text root
          → structural preflight raised through Component.raise
          → buffered (<Output>) or streaming body, unchanged
          → outer catch → Err(DocumentExecution)
```

`documentWorkflow` installs the existing fail-capable `output` mode around the
whole text-root body, before the structural preflight and before the
buffered/streaming choice, so an invalid root, a buffered root and a streaming
root all settle the same way. The low-level `ErrorMode` context default stays
`print`, which is what direct expansion and component-level harnesses read
outside a document execution. Value roots keep the `throw` decision
`runValueRoot` installs for itself.

The text root's structural preflight error now goes through `Component.raise`
like every other undecided error, instead of being hand-built into a successful
text result holding an error comment. It is observed once and the root's mode
decides it.

Everything about output transport is unchanged: the per-segment streaming loop,
the `<Output>` selection buffer, the partial tail emitted from the outer catch,
teardown ordering, durability precedence and `rememberLiveFailure()`. The change
is settlement, not transport.

## Review guide

**Start with:** `packages/core/src/execute.ts` — `documentWorkflow`, the
`scopedExpansion` head.

**Then review:**

1. `specs/executable-mdx-spec.md` §5.4 "Text roots and value roots" and §6.9's
   error-mode table — the contract.
2. `packages/core/src/errors.ts` — `ProjectedContentError`, and where `<File>`
   and `expandFunctionComponent` use it.
3. `packages/core/src/expand.ts` — `accepted()` (see **Risks**).
4. `packages/core/tests/output-error-mode.test.ts` — `Tier RF`, `OM21`/`OM21b`,
   `OM22`; `packages/core/tests/file-component.test.ts` — `FL12b` and its pair.
5. The 28 migrated fixture files.

**Look carefully at:**

- `accepted()` in `expand.ts`, which exists to keep `<Test>` containment.
- `ProjectedContentError` in `errors.ts`, how `<File>` chooses between it and
  `FileAccessError`, and the branch that recognizes it in
  `expandFunctionComponent`. Ownership is decided by the thrown class, on one
  read of the thrown object — never by searching a cause graph.

## What must stay true

- **`<PrintErrors>` is the only document-authored recovery** — enforced by the
  ledger from #442 being reachable only through core's own calls, checked by
  `OM5g`, `OM5k`, `OM5l`, `OM5n`, `OM5r`.
- **`printErrors(fn)` decides only its own component's failure** — enforced by
  `usePrintErrors("component")` delegating a content-origin failure outward,
  checked by `RF5`, `OM5d`, `OM15b`, `OM22`.
- **Describing a caller's failure does not claim it** — enforced by
  `ProjectedContentError` carrying the region's decision and the invocation
  boundary reporting it with `origin: "content"`, checked by `OM21`, `FL12b`
  and `FL12b-throw`.
- **A component that recovers and then fails on its own terms owns that
  failure** — enforced by recognizing the thrown class rather than its causes,
  checked by `FL12c` and `OM21b`.
- **Canonical `<Test>` contains** — enforced by `containedLedger` plus
  `accepted()` reading the *inherited* ledger, checked by `testing-mode.test.ts`
  and the `OM5p`/`OM5q` pair.
- **An unbound nonzero exec is a checked root failure** — unchanged from #442,
  checked by `OM5f`, `D3`, `FG7`.
- **A bound `exec as=` status is ordinary data** — unchanged from #448, checked
  by `OM20` and `RF4`.
- **`<Output>` selects rendered content and buffers a root that declares one** —
  checked by `OM1`, `OM17` and the buffered-root tests, none of which were
  weakened.

## How to verify it

- `RF1` proves an uncaught eval failure at a root with no `<Output>` fails,
  keeps the streamed prefix, starts neither the prose nor the block after it,
  and is observed exactly once. Fails if settlement is installed after the body
  branch, or if the diagnostic is reported twice.
- `RF2` proves the same region inside `<PrintErrors>` prints once and continues.
  Fails if the root mode shadowed the boundary's.
- `RF3` proves a successful root without `<Output>` still emits its complete body
  segment by segment. Fails if the root became buffered.
- `RF4` proves a bound nonzero status is data the document renders, and that a
  classifier throwing after it fails the root. Fails if #448's binding regressed.
- `RF6` proves the failure and partial output replay from the record with nothing
  appended and no command run again.
- `IE24` (`xmd run -e`, real subprocess) proves exit 1, the prefix on stdout, the
  later output absent, and the diagnostic on stderr exactly once. No core test
  reaches that boundary.
- `TD17`/`TD17b` prove a caller-content failure inside `<TempDir>` at a plain
  root fails the run, starts neither probe, and still removes the directory —
  and that `<PrintErrors>` around the same region continues and still cleans up.
- `OM21` proves an unhandled caller-content failure projected through `<File>`
  at a plain root reaches no provider, ends the run `Err` carrying `<File>`'s
  sentence and the underlying diagnostic, is observed exactly once, and renders
  no later sibling. Fails if `<File>`'s translation is treated as its own
  recovery. `OM21b` proves the authored-recovery half still continues.
- `FL12b` proves the account carries the caller's decision by identity and
  reports it once; `FL12b-throw` proves a `throw` decision travels alone;
  `FL12c` proves content that merely printed leaves the refusal `<File>`'s own.
  Together they fail if ownership is inferred from a cause chain.
- `WFC6` proves a failing workflow document reports `failed`, exits 1, and
  replays as failed, now without an `<Output>` written only to force a failure.

Manual:

```bash
deno task setup
deno task test packages/core/tests/output-error-mode.test.ts packages/core/tests/execute.test.ts \
  packages/core/tests/eval-bindings.test.ts packages/core/tests/eval-durable.test.ts \
  packages/core/tests/root-props.test.ts packages/core/tests/temp-dir.test.ts \
  packages/testing/tests/testing-mode.test.ts
deno task test packages/cli/tests/inline-cli.test.ts packages/cli/tests/workflow-cli.test.ts
deno task test --changed
```

Results on `834fedc`, with the review's own command set
(`output-error-mode`, `file-component`, `temp-dir`, `testing-mode`):
`15 passed (160 steps)`, `2 passed (36 steps)`, `294 passed (2245 steps)`.
`deno task lint` and `git diff --check` are also clean.

## Scope

### Included

- Text-root failure settlement, and the structural preflight routed through the
  ordinary raise path.
- The `<Test>` containment correction the new root mode exposed.
- Caller-content ownership through `<File>`: an account of a decided caller
  failure is settled by the caller's region, while `<File>`-owned failures —
  missing reads, path refusals, provider results, a document holding a printed

The attic, the roof and all three houses.  No code: the plumbing is #133/#134
and the sizing is #136, so these are five files and one assertion.

  bj-attic.glb              25.8MB   99,446 tris
  bj-roof.glb               26.3MB   99,568 tris
  bj-house-maitland.glb     27.5MB   93,510 tris
  bj-house-deetz.glb        27.2MB   93,528 tris
  bj-house-beetlejuice.glb  27.9MB   93,502 tris

Every one passes every budget: 1 material, 1 primitive, ONE DRAW CALL, no stray
lights, well inside the 150,000 RULING BP raised the triangle cap to.

WHICH HOUSE IS WHICH WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED.  All three came out of the tool
named deetz_house and they are geometrically IDENTICAL - same bounding box to
three decimals, triangle counts within 26 of each other - so the paint is the
only thing that tells them apart.  The base-colour PNG was decoded out of each
file and characterised:

  ...736   warmth (mean R-B) +15.3   94% red/orange        -> MAITLAND
  ...721   warmth             -4.4   red 48/violet 22/blue -> DEETZ
  ...729   warmth            -10.9   blue 49% violet 36%   -> BEETLEJUICE

The ordering on warmth is unambiguous and independently matches what STATE.md
recorded.  If it is ever wrong it is a rename, not a rebuild.

ONE NEW ASSERTION, and it is about Pages rather than about the models: every
.glb on disk is really IN THE INDEX, and assets/ holds nothing no manifest
entry fetches.  A model sitting on disk and missing from git works perfectly on
this machine and is simply absent on Pages - against a fallback that is silent
BY DESIGN, so the symptom would be "the sets never arrived" with nothing
anywhere saying why.  Same reasoning and same method as the recordings under
RULING BI: ask git, do not read the directory.

It deliberately does not demand all nine.  A set he has not modelled is a
normal state the stand-in covers; there-but-untracked is not.

It also checks the bytes survive a checkout.  `* text=auto eol=lf` decides
binary by CONTENT HEURISTIC and .gitattributes already names *.glb for exactly
this reason (it was added before a single model existed) - this checks the
result rather than the rule, by asking git whether the worktree still matches
the index.  Reading the whole porcelain line would have failed on a freshly
staged file; only the second column answers the question.

Negative-checked the real way round: it was written and run BEFORE git add and
named all five as on-disk-but-untracked.

18/18 before and after.  The build is untouched - no src/ change, so
the-house.html is byte-identical to #136's.

---

**Chain: PR 2 of 6. Merge #136 FIRST** — it is the parent of this branch, and without its sizing fix these five land cropped and poking into the auditorium.

**One thing worth your call, not taken here:** each file carries a **4096 normal map that the import throws away on arrival** (RULING BP shrinks it to 2048), so roughly 55 MB of the 135 MB a Quest downloads for these five is discarded on load. Re-encoding to 2048 JPEG would take the delivery to a few MB per file. It is the same class of fix as the texture shrink, but it **rewrites your asset** rather than changing what we do with it, so it is yours to say. Say the word and it is one PR.

body:
## What

Adds `--mode intraday-backtest` — the out-of-sample check the intraday entries previously lacked. `--mode validate` backtests the **daily composite** only, so neither the opening-range **breakout** nor the **sweep-reclaim** reversal had an automated OOS gate (called out as a known gap in #50). This replays those deterministic entries bar-by-bar on historical intraday bars.

## How a trade is simulated (no look-ahead)

1. **Decision** — at each bar T the evaluator sees only bars up to T (a bounded trailing window; it internally slices to T's session). Same bars in, same decision out.
2. **Fill** — a bar-T signal fills at bar **T+1's open**, and only when T+1 is in the **same session**. A signal on a session's last bar is dropped (can't enter and exit same day).
3. **Manage intrabar** — **stop-first** (if the bar's low pierced the stop, assume it filled first, at `min(open, stop)` for gap-through), else T1/T2/T3 target partials by the bar's high — same geometry as the live plan.
4. **Flat by session end** — anything still open at the session's last bar is closed at that close. **No overnight holds** — day-trading.

Stop geometry mirrors the live plans: breakout stops an ATR-multiple below entry; sweep-reclaim stops just below the swept wick (absolute level). A degenerate reclaim whose stop sits at/above the fill is **skipped**, the same guard `build_sweep_reclaim_plan` applies.

## Metrics & honesty

Trade-based (what validates an *entry*): **expectancy in R**, profit factor, win rate, avg win/loss R, avg hold, exit breakdown — plus a fixed-fractional-risk equity curve (total return / max drawdown). The acceptance check **refuses to bless a sub-`min_trades` sample** (default 30). `bias_disclosures` name the limits: intrabar stop-first ordering, no cross-position concurrency, and short/provider-dependent intraday data.

**Costs dominate tight stops** — the harness surfaces this: with 0.1% commission + 0.1% slippage per side, a stop on a ~$100 name with ~$2 risk fills near **−1.2R**, not −1R. That ~0.2R round-trip drag is real and is exactly why a chart read isn't a backtest.

## Files

- `src/backtest/intraday_engine.py` — `backtest_intraday` + `simulate_intraday_ticker`
- `bot.py` — `--mode intraday-backtest`, `--entry {breakout,sweep_reclaim}`, `--interval`
- `config.yaml` `intraday_backtest:` + `INTRADAY_BACKTEST_*` accessors
- `tests/test_intraday_backtest.py` (12) — deterministic mechanics via an injected strategy (next-open fill, ~−1.2R stop incl. costs, target R, session-flat, overnight-drop, one-position, metrics math) + real breakout/sweep integration
- `docs/INTRADAY_BACKTEST.md`; `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/SWEEP_RECLAIM.md` updated

## Scope / honesty

Necessary, not sufficient: a green verdict still has to survive paper (`/api/paper-scorecard`, `/api/attribution`) before real money. Intraday history is short and provider-dependent (yfinance caps 1m ~7d, 5m ~60d), and — as with the daily validate path — a real data pull is blocked by this environment's network policy; the engine and its tests run fully offline via an injectable `fetch`.

## Verification

- `pytest` — **787 passed**, 4 deselected
- `scripts/check_imports.py` — **90/90** modules import clean
- CLI smoke: `--mode intraday-backtest` runs and reports the no-data case gracefully

author: mmokhi
body:
Fixes #123.

When a new wallet can't reach a daemon it guesses where to start scanning. The guess counted 60 second blocks from 1504387246, which is eight months before our first block, and it used that same date on every network. On mainnet it lands about 350k blocks past the tip. On a test chain that is days old it lands millions past it. The wallet then scans nothing and shows an empty balance, which is the "new wallet shows no transactions, restoring from seed fixes it" report.

It counts from the real first block now. On the test chains it doesn't guess at all, because they get relaunched from scratch so no date hardcoded here stays true, and they are short enough to scan from the beginning.

Creating a wallet offline used to start at ~4.65M on mainnet and ~4.6M on testnet. It now starts at 4308795 on mainnet, against a tip around 4.35M, and at 0 on testnet.

One correction to the issue: this isn't block time drift. Our lifetime average is 60.1s against a 60s target, so drift is only about 7k blocks of the error and the wrong date is the other 346k. That also means recalibrating holds, it costs about 900 blocks a year against the 43200 block margin the caller already subtracts.

I left out defaulting mainnet to 0 when the daemon is down. It is the safest option in the issue but it would make every wallet created offline rescan 4.3M blocks, and the corrected date already lands 38k below the tip.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements Workstream 24 by replacing the runtime `pgvector`/`document_chunks` + manual wikilink graph implementation with a `lightrag-hku==1.5.6` backend in `apps/ai`, while keeping canonical Markdown as the source of truth and preserving workspace isolation.

### What changed

- **`apps/ai`** is now a LightRAG-backed FastAPI service with endpoints:
  - `POST /index`, `DELETE /index/{workspace_id}/{document_id}`
  - `POST /query`, `POST /ask`
  - `GET /graph/{workspace_id}`, `GET /index-status/{workspace_id}`
  - `GET /health`, `GET /ready`
- LightRAG is configured with Postgres-backed storage (`PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`, `PGTableGraphStorage`) on the existing `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` image — no Apache AGE or Neo4j is added.
- Each workspace gets its own `LightRAG` instance keyed by `workspace=workspace_id`; instances are cached in an LRU cache and `finalize_storages()` is awaited before eviction.
- Embedding provider defaults to `sentence-transformers` but also supports `openai` and a stable MD5-based `stub` for local smoke tests.
- No-LLM fallback is preserved: when `LLM_BASE_URL`/`LLM_API_KEY` are unset, indexing skips KG extraction (`process_options="F!"`) and `/ask`/`/query` fall back to grounded naive retrieval.
- **`apps/api`** delegates `search.ts`, `ask.ts`, `graph.ts`, `documents.ts`, and `propose.ts` to `apps/ai`; `document_chunks` writes and `chunks.ts` are removed.
- **`apps/web`** graph click handling now skips entity nodes (they no longer navigate to a non-existent note).
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` AD-003, `docs/WORKSTREAMS.md`, `docs/GAUNTLET_LOG.md` Round 2.0, and `.env.example` are updated.

author: joseph-cursio
body:
## What

`SwiftFormatConfig` promises an exact round trip in two docstrings. It does not have one.

`parseLine` classifies a line by its **trimmed** content, so a whitespace-only line becomes `.blank`, and `.blank.rendered` is `""`. The spaces are dropped:

```swift
SwiftFormatConfig.parse("--indent 4\n   \n--enable isEmpty").serialized()
// "--indent 4\n\n--enable isEmpty"   — the three spaces are gone
```

Every other line shape is reproduced byte-for-byte, including comments and directives with leading or irregular internal whitespace.

## Why it wasn't caught

Two tests assert the exact round trip and pass. Neither samples a whitespace-only line — `sample` has genuinely empty lines and `roundTripEdges` has an indented comment, and both of those *are* preserved. The tests are green, correct about their inputs, and cannot fail for the reason the docstring is wrong.

Renamed the broader one to `"Parsing then serializing round-trips this sample exactly"`, with a comment recording why it passes and where the general claim now lives.

## The laws

`SwiftFormatConfigNormalFormPropertyTests` — 6 tests, ~2,500 generated inputs, seeded so any failure is replayable from the seed in its message.

| law | status |
|---|---|
| exact round trip, restricted to inputs with no whitespace-only line | **the strong law** — rejects any change that stops preserving `raw` |
| normal form: `serialized(parse(·))` reaches a fixed point in one pass | true unconditionally, but **weak** — any stable normalisation satisfies it |
| the counterexample to the strong law | pinned, so it isn't "strengthened" back |

The distinction between the first two is the point. Normalising twice is a no-op the moment normalising once is stable, so the normal-form law is satisfied by implementations that mangle their input. Restricting the domain instead of weakening the law keeps the property that the type actually promises.

## Mutation-checked

A passing property test is worth nothing until it's shown it can fail. Three reversible edits to the production code:

| mutant | issues raised |
|---|---|
| comment stores `trimmed`, not `raw` | 227 |
| option renders from key/value, not `raw` | 211 |
| `.blank` renders `" "` instead of `""` | 249 |

Production file restored byte-identical afterwards; suite green on unmutated code.

## Scope

**No production behaviour changes.** Whether dropping trailing whitespace on an otherwise-empty line is a defect is a judgement for you — it's defensible normalisation. What isn't defensible is a docstring promising it doesn't happen, so the behaviour is documented rather than altered. If you'd rather `.blank` preserved its raw text, that's a one-line change and the pinned counterexample test is where it would flip.

## Notes

- The generator is hand-rolled rather than a new dependency, and deliberately avoids a `RandomNumberGenerator` conformance: this package sets `.defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)`, which would make `next()` main-actor isolated and unable to satisfy that protocol's nonisolated requirement.
- The 6 failures in `OptionRuleUsage Integration` on `main` are pre-existing and unrelated — verified by running that suite with this branch's new file removed. They compare a curated table against the installed SwiftFormat catalog.
- `SwiftFormatRuleStudioCore/.swiftinfer/` is left untracked and not added here; it's tool artifacts and probably wants a `.gitignore` entry.

Closes the drift `presence-sync.py --check` has been reporting against the live site:

```
Portfolio  DRIFT  Solstice Solutions, Inc. start date: yaml=2025-11 portfolio=2025-10
Portfolio  DRIFT  Infosysnow Inc. end date: yaml=2025-11 portfolio=2025-10
exit 1
```

**SEVIS is the authority for OPT employment dates** and settles both:

| SEVIS employer | record | dates |
|---|---|---|
| 11873739 | Solstice | 11/18/2025 – ongoing |
| 11698556 | Infosysnow | 08/11/2025 – 11/17/2025 |

| Role | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| Solstice | Oct 2025 – Present | **Nov 2025 – Present** |
| Infosysnow | Aug 2025 – **Oct** 2025 | Aug 2025 – **Nov** 2025 |

The two are continuous — 17 Nov ends, 18 Nov begins — as OPT requires.

#44 carries this same date fix, but on `fix/dates-and-positioning`, a branch that **also removes 31 project cards**. author: naturalclar
body:
The first Link check run ([#31940347770](https://github.com/Naturalclar/blog.naturalclar.dev/actions/runs/31940347770)) found seven 404s. Two of them were **ours**:

```
- https://blog.naturalclar.dev/react-native-review-2019/     in: future-of-react-native, react-native-review-2020
- https://blog.naturalclar.dev/whats-new-in-react-native-0.62/  in: whats-coming-up-in-react-native-0.63
```

That is the Gatsby URL shape. This site serves `/posts/{slug}/`, so those three links (two distinct URLs) have pointed at nothing since the migration — three articles cross-referencing each other, all dead, and nothing was watching.

## The fix, and the trap in the fix

They are relative now — `/posts/react-native-review-2019/` — which cannot rot when the domain or the host changes again.

But that would also have **taken them out of the checker's reach**: nothing relative needs fetching, so `check-links.mjs` skipped anything not starting with `http`. Fixing the three links and stopping there would have quietly reduced coverage, and the next occurrence of exactly this bug would have gone unreported.

So `collectLinks` now returns internal links too, and `checkInternal` verifies `/posts/{slug}/` against `content/blog/` — a typo in a slug lands in the **broken** bucket and fails the run, the same as a dead host. No network involved, so it costs nothing.

Only `/posts/` is verified. `/page/N/` and `/tags/x/` are generated from data this script would have to duplicate to know about, and no article links to one; those report as `ok — not verified` rather than pretending. `--host=` drops internal links from the run, since narrowing to one host is not a request to see them again.

## Verification

**Fixture** (real HTTP server, plus the two new internal cases):

```
checking 9 external and 3 internal link(s) in content/blog/
## Broken (3)
- /posts/no-such-post/   no post named no-such-post   in: post-a   <- new
- .../gone 404, .../boom 500
6 ok, 3 broken, 1 unreachable, 1 moved, 1 refused                  <- exit 1
```

`/posts/post-b/` passes and `/tags/memo/` reports `not verified` — neither is a false alarm.

**Real archive:** `checking 126 external and 2 internal link(s)` — 128 total, unchanged, with the two former `blog.naturalclar.dev` URLs having moved from the external side to the internal one. Neither is reported as a problem.

**Build:** `out/posts/react-native-review-2019/index.html` and `out/posts/whats-new-in-react-native-0.62/index.html` both exist, and the three rewritten links render as `href="/posts/…/"` pointing at them. `grep` for `blog.naturalclar.dev/` across `content/` returns nothing.

`pnpm lint` clean.

## Still open from that run

The other five broken links are external and each needs a judgement call, so they are not in this PR: `twitter.com/chatsidhartha`, `reactnavigation.org/docs/en/next/getting-started.html`, `facebook/react-native/issues/23313`, the Turbo Modules proposal, and a `StyleSheet.js#L255` line link that broke when `master` became `main`. One `unreachable`: `teabreak.e-spres-oh.com` no longer resolves at all.

Refs #123

author: allingtm
body:
Full feature and experience parity with the finalized reference pair (`docs/video-upload-and-streaming.md` §5, `docs/posting-on-poor-networks.md`), per the reviewed plan in `docs/plans/2026-08-15-flutter-video-ux-parity-queued-posts.md`. Entirely client-side — no schema or server changes.

## Flutter: video experience parity
- Staged processing tile fed by the real transcode progress stream (`Preparing your video…` / `Compressing to 720p… N%` / `Creating your cover image…`), exact notice copy, 1 s duration grace.
- **WYSIWYG cover picker**: whole-second slider, frames captured from the original file (platform-units workaround), preview shows the captured bytes — never a live scrubber — guarded by a monotonic generation counter.
- Draft tile with duration + `Change cover` chips (inert, not hidden, while in flight); posting step labels; per-state feed pills (error pill now visible to everyone).
- **Inline playback in the feed tile** via one shared player: sound on, always-visible mute, tap-to-pause, freeze-on-end with replay glyph, display-only progress bar, texture sized from the controller aspect ratio, one-tile-at-a-time coordinator.

## Flutter: posting on poor networks
Scope decisions settled with the owner: **foreground-only** (consequence of one-time upload URLs) and a **single-slot queue**.
- Whole-submit weather/answer classifier; flat 60 s timeout on the multipart commit; fresh-URL-on-retry unchanged.
- Versioned queued-post model resuming from the first incomplete step; idempotency key preserved across retries and relaunches.
- Disk store with **media custody** (sandbox copies, identical-clip skip, missing-media refusal), atomic replace, 7-day max age, restore-backs-off, sign-out clear.
- Sender with three triggers — connectivity offline→online **edge**, app resume, capped 30s/2m/5m/15m backoff (cap stops ticking, keeps the queue) — bootstrapped at app root covering the documented Riverpod pitfalls.
- UX contract: `Waiting for network — this will post automatically.`, edit reclaims custody, discard clears disk, posted notice via a running sent counter.
- Two-tier retry: thread mutes and keyed comment creates get in-request transient retry; **reactions excluded after audit** — the endpoint is toggle-semantic, so a retried silently-landed toggle would undo the tap.

## Web
- `Change cover` in the web composer: slider-driven seek + capture of the displayed frame (WYSIWYG by construction), one shared capture implementation with the default poster path.

## Testing
- Flutter: **454 tests, 0 failures**; `flutter analyze` clean. New coverage: store custody/aging/restore rules, sender schedule/cap/edge-vs-level/overlap, classifier table, cover-picker generation counter, play-session end/replay, composer queued states, posted-notice listener.
- Webapp: `tsc --noEmit` clean; 216 passing (only the 7 known pre-existing `registration-screening` failures); 10 new capture-controller tests.
- Manual device pass still to run with the mobile release: park-story queue→pocket→resume→auto-post, kill-mid-upload→relaunch restore, cover WYSIWYG on both platforms, iOS silent-switch behaviour.

author: nstfkc
body:
Found by the adversarial review of #411. **Pre-existing on `main`** — not introduced by that PR — but #411's `_count: true` routes through the discarded rewrite, so it has to land first.

## The defect

`$execute` scopes arguments in two passes:

```ts
let effective = args;

// pass 1 — pushes each reached model's scope down into the argument tree
effective = applyNestedPolicies(schema, effective, currentUser(), system, …);

// pass 2 — scopes the root
if (policies.length > 0) {
  if (!preScoped) {
    effective = applyPolicies(policies, policy, args, …);  // <-- `args`, not `effective`
  }
}
```

`applyPolicies` builds its result by spreading its input (`{ ...args, where: scope }`), so passing `args` overwrites `effective` and throws away everything pass 1 wrote: the scope pushed into every `include`, every `_count`, every relation filter and every relation ordering.

The fix is one word — `args` → `effective`.

## Why it survived

The trigger is `policies.length > 0` on the **root** model. With an unpolicied root the whole block is skipped and pass 1 survives intact, which is exactly the configuration every nested-policy test uses. The headline test states it outright:

> Note `User` is deliberately *unpolicied* here, so the only thing that can scope the accounts is `Account`'s own policy firing on a nested read.

Policy on the child alone is covered from several angles across `policies.test.ts`, `nested-write-policies.test.ts` and `relation-filter-policies.test.ts`. Policy on **both** — the ordinary multi-tenant shape, where the tenant model is scoped and so are its children — was covered by nothing.

The seed could not have caught it either, even with the root policied. Alice owns exactly one account and it is already in her organisation, so an unscoped include returns the correct rows by accident. The new tests give her a second account **in Bob's organisation** — hers, in his tenant — which comes back if and only if the nested scope was discarded.

## Impact

Not confined to counts. Under a policied root:

| Query | Returned | Correct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include: { accounts: true }` | accounts in orgs `[1, 2]` | `[1]` |
| `_count: { select: { accounts: true } }` | `2` | `1` |

A `redact`-only policy carrying no `scope` at all reproduces it identically, which pins the trigger as "the root has any policy" rather than anything the scope does — so a root model can leak through its children while doing nothing to its own rows.

## Verification

Three regression tests in `templates/saas-starter/app/models/policies.test.ts`, as a `describe` beside the headline test: nested include, nested `_count`, and the `redact`-only root. All three **fail on the previous line and pass on this one** — confirmed by stashing the one-word change and re-running.

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| saas-starter `app/models/` | 872 passed, 134 skipped |
| `packages/gemi` ORM | 2537 passed |

No existing test changed behaviour, which is its own finding: nothing in the suite depended on the discarded rewrite, and nothing caught its absence.
